# Development roadmap

The current game has **nine flyable craft and implemented slices across Phases 2–10**, including remapping/curves/glyphs, bounded ENet/crew integration, nearby activities and visits to Ember Moon, Aurora and Rime. **The roadmap is not complete.** Phase 1 authenticity research and the full station, fleet, combat, multiplayer, planetary and release scope remain open. A checked item records bounded implementation or research, never whole-phase completion or historical authentication.

## Current completion assessment — 2026-10-13

**Completion answer:** this is a playable development project with substantial implementation, but substantial production and release work remains. **All ten phase exit gates remain open. The consolidated checklist contains 35 tasks: one completed and 34 remaining.** The next achievable milestone is an integrated, fully accepted packaged baseline; finishing that milestone does not finish the original fleet, station/world content, multiplayer or human/hardware acceptance. No defensible percentage or finish date is available until the required roster, owners and estimates are agreed.

### Phase status and distance to completion

**None of the ten phases has met its full exit gate.** Implementation is substantial, but the remaining work spans production content, integration and release acceptance. A reliable percentage or finish date needs a fixed final roster and measured delivery estimates; checkbox counts would give false precision.

The completion work has three distinct parts: finish the named runtime/content gaps, accept the implemented game through normal-controls play on supported hardware, and qualify the exact release package. An unchecked item may already have working implementation; read its remaining acceptance condition before assigning new code. The original phase requirements are reconciled by the [completion backlog](#remaining-tasks-to-complete-the-project) below. Phase-to-task mapping: Phase 1 → §0/§7; Phase 2 → §1/§6; Phase 3 → §2/§7; Phase 4 → §2/§7; Phase 5 → §2; Phase 6 → §2/§3/§4; Phase 7 → §4; Phase 8 → §3; Phase 9 → §1/§5/§6; Phase 10 → §1–§6. Licensing and final-candidate acceptance in §6 apply across the phases.

**Distance to done:** substantial production work and qualification remain. Matching Windows/Linux `75de4c4bb` alpha checkpoints include the qualified sustained-carriage repair, startup and bounded shared/home-route acceptance. Source body176 passes with 0.001435 m maximum drift against the unchanged 0.05 m limit; ordinary shared127 and packed shared132 pass. Full canonical remote-crew journeys, main integration and complete candidate acceptance remain open. The original Windows-PCK census failure is repaired: source, Windows and Linux census19 pass on checkpoint `33c96ab45`, with matching packages published. Qualify the newer shared-abandonment, recovery and crew repairs on one integrated source, then complete the named content/runtime gaps, uninterrupted play, native hardware, human review, installed recovery, licensing and signing. A finish date requires the scope, dependencies, owners and estimates in §0.

Parallel work does not waive the original phase exit gates or mark unperformed human playtests complete; the Phase 2 uninterrupted-play gate remains outstanding despite existing later-phase implementation. Every implementation task follows the existing [work-item contract](#required-work-item-contract), produces a running-game or packaging outcome, and uses the smallest existing regression that protects it.

### What must happen before the project can be called done

The remaining work includes missing product delivery as well as acceptance of existing features. The 34 remaining tasks (35 total) below are the authoritative checklist; this sequence groups them without adding duplicate tasks.

1. **Set the complete release scope (§0, §7).** Record the required station routes, original fleet, modern craft, activities, worlds, multiplayer limits and desktop targets. Keep missing historical evidence and shared multiplayer planetary travel as explicit dependencies or owner decisions.
2. **Close runtime blockers (§1, §3, §4, §6).** The reviewed missed-start race fix is packaged in `79d5154`; accept the implemented race/Patrol recovery, accept the published Convoy missed-start payment/reset fix, and cover remaining shipped reward-bearing activities and ambiguous legacy data safely. Investigate the intermittent remote landing failure, finish unsupported shipped multiplayer paths and test actual in-world interruption with usable craft/seat recovery.
3. **Finish the agreed content (§2, §3, §7).** Deliver the remaining station/fleet/world content, animation, combat roles, art and authored audio. Verify physical routes and repeatable activity loops through ordinary player controls.
4. **Pass real-play and hardware acceptance (§1, §3–§5).** Complete uninterrupted solo/planetary journeys, native multiplayer and soak, first-time-player tuning, GPU benchmarks, physical-controller/accessibility checks and visual/listening review. Fix findings and repeat affected scenarios.
5. **Qualify the final distributed build (§6).** Freeze one source, pass its complete regression and required graphical reviews, test final install/update/rollback/crash recovery on supported platforms, finish licensing/trusted signing and publish matching artifacts. Close every P0/P1 and disposition remaining P2 findings.

A focused test or successful menu startup closes only its stated contract. Required content, end-to-end play, native performance and human reviews still need their own acceptance results.

### Definition of project completion

Close the consolidated tasks above only when their acceptance conditions hold. Then reconcile each original Phase 1–10 open item against the delivered game: mark it complete with bounded source/build and acceptance references, or record an explicit owner-approved scope deferral beside it. Historical checkpoint notes remain historical. The final distributed candidate must satisfy the release gates, have zero open P0/P1 defects and reviewed P2 dispositions, and match the tested artifacts. Any deferred original scope remains visible; a milestone release does not silently fulfill it.

## Implementation strategy — playable core first

The phase and feature lists below remain the complete intended scope. This strategy changes **execution order and acceptance discipline**, not the destination. Work proceeds in small vertical increments: stabilize the current packaged game, add one bounded feature slice, restore every stability gate, then produce the next playtest build. A later phase may be researched or prototyped in isolation, but it does not displace unresolved core-loop defects.

### Priority order

1. **P0 — cannot continue safely:** editor/import failure, crash, corrupted save/configuration, invalid package, unrecoverable soft-lock, authority duplication, or a regression that can destroy or permanently strand gameplay state. Stop other implementation until reproduced, fixed, and package-verified.
2. **P1 — core loop blocked or misleading:** cannot reach a required route without an unintended jump, visible walkable surface lacks collision, interaction/boarding cannot be acquired from its intended approach, character or craft presentation contradicts authoritative movement, landing cannot be acquired reasonably, required prompts are absent, or a texture/material defect systematically reverses or destroys scene readability. P1 work takes precedence over new art, rooms, ships, weapons, or activities.
3. **P2 — playable but materially rough:** camera discomfort, poor control tuning, unclear feedback, local clipping, isolated visual mismatch, weak mix, avoidable friction, or recoverable lifecycle inconsistency. Batch these into short polish passes between P1 closure and the next content slice.
4. **P3 — expansion and optional polish:** new modules, ships, combat breadth, multiplayer, destinations, decorative density, and speculative fidelity improvements. These remain planned below and resume only while the active prototype gate is green.

Bug status is independent from severity: `CANDIDATE` → `NEW` → `REPRODUCED` → `FIXING` → `VERIFYING` → `CLOSED`. Use `NOT_REPRODUCED` when the recorded scenario produces zero failures in ten attempts across two documented configurations; use `ACCEPTED_RISK` only with rationale and owner. Never mark an unreproduced report closed. Every intake record includes stable ID/title, reporter/date, first/last affected source and artifact hashes, OS/CPU/GPU/RAM/driver/audio/input/resolution/profile, clean or retained user-data state, numbered steps, expected/actual result, failure frequency, affected loop beat, log/image/video paths and hashes, severity, owner, linked reproducer/regression, and disposition.

### Stabilization stages

1. **Gate A — reproducible baseline:** add a checked-in one-command runner that recursively discovers `tests/**/*_test.gd`, freezes the sorted roster, gives each suite a timeout, requires exit `0` and exactly one accepted terminal sentinel, counts anchored assertions, scans raw logs for failure/error/leak/orphan diagnostics, hashes every log/result file, and proves the runnable-source manifest is unchanged before/after. Use the runner-discovered sorted roster rather than a hard-coded suite total. Historical matrices remain in the dated archive; Gate A requires a new source-pinned record.
2. **Gate B — stabilization closure:** reproduce or explicitly disposition every active P0/P1 and current review candidate. Each closed defect needs a before-failing/after-green regression, focused and full matrix, current-package scenario rerun, and independent verification for P0/P1.
3. **Gate C — packaged core scenarios:** run three scripts without debug shortcuts. **Guided:** cold boot → begin → walk/board Torrent → apply thrust for same-tick automatic power → physical launch → targets/defender → lease landing → `1.5` physics seconds of neutral automatic shutdown → disembark → completion. **Sandbox:** traverse Central/Aft/Habitat/Freight/Fleet Dock; launch/land/exit Arrow, Jovian, Zenith, Halyard, Bulwark and all three Cinder craft; deliberately crash; recover on foot; regenerate and reuse a craft. **Settings/re-entry:** save settings → restart → pause/resume → camera modes → all required keyboard/mouse and current gamepad lifecycle controls. Require Guided 3/3 consecutive fresh-process passes, Sandbox 1/1, Settings 1/1.
4. **Gate D — external tuning:** five first-time Windows players may use in-game help but receive no developer intervention. At least four must launch, fight, redock, and disembark within 30 minutes; median camera comfort, control clarity, and landing clarity must each be at least 4/5; any P0/P1 returns the project to Gate B.
5. **Gate E — candidate/performance:** export from one exact clean commit with a unique build label. Record source commit, matrix record, Godot version, EXE size/hash, PE version, embedded PCK inventory, signing state, smoke result, and hardware. Initial proposed 1920×1080 High benchmark after 60 seconds warm-up: ten-minute representative route, p95 ≤16.7 ms, p99 ≤33.3 ms, no post-warm-up frame >100 ms, peak working set ≤4 GiB. Record CPU/GPU/RAM/driver/audio device; these are design budgets until representative hardware validates them.
6. **Gate F — controlled expansion resume:** all nine current craft/package scenarios, frozen matrix, external thresholds, performance candidate, zero P0/P1, and no accepted core-loop P2. Resume the existing Phase 1–9 backlog with a WIP limit of one authority-bearing runtime slice. Every merged runtime slice invalidates relevant package/human evidence and returns through the affected gates before the next slice.

Pause expansion again on any P0/P1, editor/import or full-matrix failure, two open core-loop P2s in one subsystem, Guided below 3/3, external completion below 4/5, same-hardware p95 regression above 10%, or mismatched source/artifact evidence. Fixes may cut an immediate candidate, but otherwise produce at most one internal candidate after a clean day and one public preview only after two consecutive candidate gates; permission/legal/licensing and signing requirements still apply.

### Required work-item contract

Every implementation item—bug fix or feature—must record the following before it can be called complete:

- **Player-visible outcome:** one sentence describing what the player can now do or perceive.
- **Authority owner:** the exact node/resource responsible for state. Presentation may observe authority but must not silently duplicate collision, damage, leases, movement, scoring, interaction, or regeneration.
- **Implementation seam:** the smallest existing component/API to change; new parallel systems require an explicit reason.
- **Reproduction or scenario:** deterministic starting state, input sequence, expected result, and failure witness. A bug begins with a failing witness; a feature begins with an acceptance scenario.
- **Focused regression:** a permanent test against the production scene/component, including at least one structured-red mutation or boundary case when the feature has authority or lifecycle risk.
- **Integration regression:** the complete affected player path through real `Main`, not only an isolated fixture.
- **Package parity:** the source fix is not accepted for a downloadable prototype until the exported Windows pack reproduces the corrected behaviour or passes an equivalent external probe.
- **Human check:** controls, visual readability, texture direction, audio audibility, and comfort require real-time review; headless assertions do not substitute for perception.

Unconfirmed audit observations stay in [`bugs.md`](bugs.md) until reproduced. Confirmed P0/P1 defects move into the active Phase 2 stabilization checkpoint with a failing witness and owner; resolved items remain recorded with their regression gate instead of being silently deleted.

### Playable-prototype gate

The next expansion slice may begin only when one fresh, source-pinned Windows candidate satisfies all of these conditions:

- Boots into the title and starts a shift without `ERROR`, `SCRIPT ERROR`, `FATAL`, rejection, orphan, resource-leak, or invalid-authority diagnostics.
- The on-foot avatar visibly faces its actual horizontal velocity for forward, back, strafe, and diagonal movement at multiple camera headings; input/velocity must not be reversed to compensate for art orientation.
- A no-cheat traversal from spawn reaches the Central berth, Aft upper level, Habitat, Freight branch, and Fleet Dock walking surfaces without falling through, snagging on decorative treads, or requiring an undocumented jump. Every broad route surface that visually reads as floor/deck/ramp must have immediate World collision support or explicit non-walkable presentation metadata.
- Station floor/wall/stair materials use a coherent station material family with continuous metric mapping; ship-specific atlases stay on their registered ships. Authored UV0 surfaces have non-degenerate, consistent outward-view handedness and bounded texel-density distortion.
- All nine production ships can be approached from collision-clear routes, boarded through the production reservation path, powered by same-tick flight demand, launched, flown, fired where their role supports it, returned with forgiving assist acquisition, strictly docked, idled automatically offline after exactly `1.5` neutral physics seconds, and exited. Destroy/recover/switch-craft reuse must not duplicate authority or strand a berth. Dock 04/05/06 are physical `ShipBerth` children owned by `FleetExpansionBerths` and indexed into the same world lease table as the original fleet.
- The guided Torrent loop completes only after its actual combat, return, dock, automatic engine-offline, and disembark lifecycle, once per generation.
- The complete sorted `tests/**/*_test.gd` matrix passes in isolated processes after a clean editor/import gate, with exact terminal sentinels and no unreviewed diagnostics.
- A human completes at least one uninterrupted packaged sortie using normal controls—no harness teleport, direct state mutation, or debugger shortcut—and records control, camera, collision, texture, prompt, audio, and performance observations.

### Content-slice cadence

After the gate above is green, each feature slice follows this order: **specification → isolated implementation → focused tests → production integration → physical player-path test → rendered/audio review → full matrix → packaged smoke → human playtest**. Only one authority-bearing slice should be in integration at a time. Presentation-only asset work may run in parallel when it touches disjoint files and consumes already frozen semantic anchors. Any new P0/P1 re-enters stabilization immediately; the unfinished feature stays paused rather than being layered over a broken baseline.

### Junior developer delivery checklist

Use this sequence for every roadmap task. Do not skip directly from an isolated scene looking correct to editing `Main`.

1. Read the relevant phase specification, existing component script, scene, focused test, integration test, `RESEARCH.md`/evidence spec when historically labelled, and `ASSETS.md` when adding art/audio/material bytes.
2. Write the player-visible outcome and list the files you expect to touch. Identify the current authority owner and signal/API boundary. If ownership is unclear, stop and document it before coding.
3. Run the editor/import gate and the existing focused test once to establish a clean baseline. For a bug, add or run a deterministic failing reproduction before changing production code.
4. Implement the smallest change behind the existing public API. Avoid direct node-path access from unrelated systems when a typed getter/signal/component already exists.
5. Extend the component audit with stable IDs, exact rosters/budgets, authority flags, and structured errors. Return deep copies of mutable reports so callers cannot mutate component state.
6. Add focused tests for the normal case, exact boundary, invalid input, duplicate/re-entry/reset behaviour, and at least one mutation that must turn the audit red. Do not assert only node existence.
7. Add a production integration test through `res://scenes/main.tscn`. Drive normal inputs/components and verify the player-visible result plus unchanged adjacent authority.
8. If geometry or mapping changed, run native Forward+ at the shipping resolution/profile and inspect original-resolution frames. If audio changed, audition on real output hardware at multiple mix levels/distances.
9. Run affected neighbouring suites, then the complete isolated-process matrix. Treat new warnings, leaks, timeouts, orphan/RID diagnostics, or altered source bytes during validation as failures until explained.
10. Export from the exact tested commit, inspect the PE/PCK metadata, smoke the embedded pack from a clean directory, run external package probes where available, and complete the human scenario. Record artifact hash and outstanding limitations.

The minimum change report should state: outcome, root cause/design decision, files, tests/assertions, native/human evidence, package hash, and remaining risks. A junior developer should be able to hand that report to a reviewer without relying on unstated conversation context.

## Historical context and continuing constraints

The [dated archive](docs/history/README.md) preserves the August art passes, cabin-access notes, player recollections, session handoffs and reconciliation checkpoints, including their source/package hashes and original links. Those observations describe the checkpoint where they were recorded; no historical native startup or capture qualifies the current candidate.

Carry forward the unresolved work: improve material/lighting readability while preserving evidence-bounded layout and silhouettes; obtain authored geometry/material and human art review; re-measure the merged scene before changing performance ceilings; validate minor cargo/deck offsets through player observation; and resolve navigation continuity before expanding autonomous services. Player recollections remain research leads, never registered evidence. Existing source fixes and later settings persistence supersede stale handoff tasks. The phase lists below retain the full feature and acceptance scope.

## Phase 1 — Research

### Design and implementation specification

- Treat historical evidence as versioned input data, not prose authority embedded ad hoc in gameplay code. Add each source to `docs/research/source_ledger.json` with stable ID, URL/archive/access date, upload date, recording/build date when actually known, rendition hash/technical metadata, exact frame or timestamp anchors, rights status, and allowed claim.
- Reflect claim strength in `docs/research/ship_evidence_matrix.json` and `docs/research/STATION_TOPOLOGY.md` before changing original-labelled silhouettes or adjacency. Use the statuses `authenticated`, `bounded_partial_reconstruction`, `provisional_candidate`, `modern_interpretation`, and `unknown`; a later implementation or attractive render never upgrades historical confidence by itself.
- For a reconstruction slice, create a written evidence boundary before art: list observed macroform, conflicts, unknowns, excluded footage discontinuities, modern ergonomic normalization, and removable modern systems. The runtime wrapper must expose source-core and modern subtrees separately where practical.
- Never commit third-party footage merely to make the audit reproducible. Commit the ledger, hashes, extraction commands, and frame anchors; keep source media external unless permission explicitly allows redistribution.
- Research exit gate for any original-labelled asset: an independent reader can reproduce the name-to-model/topology claim from the ledger, the code/art metadata repeats the same bounded wording, the focused evidence test passes, and unknown dates/functions are not promoted into canonical facts.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. Add or amend the source row in `docs/research/source_ledger.json`. Use the next stable evidence ID; keep `upload_date`, `recording_date`, and `build_revision` separate; use `null`/`unknown` rather than copying an upload year into the model/build field.
2. Put every observation in a timestamp/frame-anchored claim array. Record source dimensions, fps, duration, and SHA-256 of the inspected rendition. Add an explicit exclusion boundary when a cut or discontinuity breaks identity continuity.
3. Update `docs/research/ship_evidence_matrix.json` or `docs/research/STATION_TOPOLOGY.md` with the safest claim, unresolved conflicts, current implementation status, and prohibited stronger wording. Do not infer geometry from a name-only source.
4. Write or update the asset-specific specification in `docs/`. Split it into observed source core, inferred/unknown features, modern playable normalization, semantic anchors, collision proposal status, and visual comparison views.
5. Mirror the evidence ID/status—not the whole dossier—into `ShipDefinition`, module metadata, manifest, presentation audit, and UI copy. Gameplay must remain functional if research metadata is unavailable.
6. Update `RESEARCH.md`, `ASSETS.md`, and the focused research test together. Search for superseded chronology/authentication wording across the repository before declaring the docs frozen.
7. Run `tests/research_evidence_test.gd`, JSON parsing, editor/import, and any asset-specific evidence test. Have a reviewer verify at least one claim directly from the external source ledger entry.

## Phase 2 — Vertical slice

### Design and implementation specification

- `GameFlow` coordinates the solo loop and UI phase; it must not become the physics owner of the Player, a ship, a berth, a weapon hit, or a station door. `PlayerController` owns embodied movement, `HeroShip`/ship subclasses own craft simulation, `ShipBerth` owns lease/occupancy, `ShipBoardingArea` owns access/reservation, `CombatResolver` owns accepted hit results, and presentation components consume signals without changing those results.
- Keep the playable route physical. Core acceptance uses the production `CharacterBody3D`, real collision layers, real `InputMap` actions, real boarding areas, real seat anchors, real ship commands, and real berth leases. Teleports and direct state changes may set up a test but cannot be the evidence that the route itself works.
- Keep visible and physical geometry intentionally paired. A collision-only ramp may smooth movement only when a rendered surface occupies the same plane within the player-foot tolerance; decorative tread, inset, trim, grille, or shell meshes must be explicitly tagged non-walkable. Discover broad upward-facing route meshes in addition to maintaining a curated critical-surface roster.
- Keep movement authority and model orientation separate. Camera-relative input determines desired velocity; `CharacterBody3D` moves in that direction; the active visual mount applies only the model-specific forward-axis correction. Never fix a backwards-facing model by reversing input, velocity, camera axes, or animation semantics.
- Split material families by use. Authored ship atlases remain on their registered craft; procedural station architecture uses station-specific, lighting-neutral, tileable PBR maps with module/world-stable projection; authored hero surfaces use metric UV0. Tests must pin texture identity, importer normal convention, handedness, edge continuity, texel density, and the live material bindings rather than only checking that a texture exists.
- Landing assist is acquisition and guidance, not authority bypass. A broad capture volume may brake, stage, and align a compatible ship at forgiving speed/attitude limits; the final dock still requires the strict hull envelope, unobstructed path, valid requester-bound lease, exact berth identity, and occupy-before-snap ordering.
- Boarding reach must be wide enough for collision-clear approaches and must select the nearest eligible ship deterministically. It may not enlarge station-door reach, cross an opposite hull, ignore a disabled/reserved `ShipBoardingArea`, or clear the post-exit reboard latch before leaving the full boarding envelope.
- Combat chronology is authority first, presentation at travel arrival: health/collision/scoring resolve once; pulse receipt completion releases impact/explosion/audio once; abort/recycle releases any deferred record atomically. Pools and re-entry cleanup are bounded and cannot allocate gameplay authority.
- Vertical-slice exit gate: the complete playable-prototype gate above, plus human tuning of on-foot camera, flight, landing, boarding, combat readability, audibility, and recovery in the same packaged candidate.

### Junior implementation playbook

**Know the ownership map before editing:**

- `scripts/game/game_flow.gd`: solo progression, prompts, active player/ship selection, and transitions through `INTRO → APPROACH_SHIP → BOARDING → START_ENGINES → LAUNCH → TARGET_PRACTICE → INTERCEPTOR_ENGAGEMENT → RETURN_TO_YARD → SHUT_DOWN → DISEMBARKING → COMPLETE`, with `FREE_FLIGHT`, `FAILED`, and `RECOVERING` branches.
- `scripts/player/player_controller.gd` and `scenes/player/player.tscn`: on-foot input, `CharacterBody3D` movement/collision, camera, visual yaw mount, interaction origin, boarding/disembark animation and embodied lifecycle.
- `scripts/ships/hero_ship.gd` plus ship subclass/scene: engine state, sampled `ShipCommand`, flight, cameras, seat/exit anchors, damage integration, staged landing request, telemetry, and ship-local presentation hooks.
- `scripts/interaction/ship_boarding_area.gd`: per-ship availability and reservation. `GameFlow` may select the nearest eligible area but must still reserve through this component.
- `scripts/world/ship_berth.gd`: compatible definition check, requester/ship-bound reservation token, assist capture/staging data, strict landing volume, occupancy, release, and audit.
- `scripts/combat/live_combat_authority.gd` and `scripts/combat/combat_resolver.gd`: accepted shot request and resolved result. Damage adapters own health/collision effects; pulse/audio/damage presentation scripts own visuals/sound only.
- `scripts/world/shipyard_world.gd` and module scripts: station integration, world routes, berth registry, landing-assist selection, and static collision. They do not own Player movement or ship simulation.

**Implement or repair the loop in this order:**

1. **On-foot:** add input through the `InputMap`, sample it in `PlayerController`, compute desired movement in the camera-horizontal plane, apply gravity/floor snap, call `move_and_slide()`, then rotate only `BodyPivot` toward the resulting horizontal direction. Validate W/A/S/D/diagonals at several camera yaw angles and on slopes/moving interiors.
2. **Route:** add visible deck/ramp/stair geometry and matching World-layer collision in the owning module. Make collider layer/mask explicit. Add the surface to the curated critical roster or tag it with a reason if intentionally non-walkable; confirm the discovery ray finds support under the visible top.
3. **Interaction:** put the ship's `ShipBoardingArea` at a collision-clear semantic boarding point. Candidate selection uses distance from `player.get_interaction_origin()`, filters `is_available_for(player)`, sorts by distance then stable instance/scene identity, and preserves station-door priority on actual overlap.
4. **Boarding:** reserve the area, generation-guard the asynchronous transition, disable embodied collision only after the transition owns the live seat, parent/follow the seat through the existing Player API, and release reservation/state on cancellation, destruction, detach, or reuse.
5. **Automatic demand/launch:** bind the active camera and command source once, clear parked input, and accept one authoritative `ShipCommand` per physics tick. Throttle, attitude/look, boost, brake, hover, barrel roll, landing, or fire demand must commit `ENGINE_ONLINE` before that same snapshot reaches flight/weapons; camera, pause/UI, and interaction alone must not wake it. Sustained departure input clears the berth latch, while a tap must not clear landed authority. Explicit engine request methods remain internal lifecycle/AI/test compatibility seams, not player actions.
6. **Flight/fire:** populate one `ShipCommand` snapshot per physics tick, validate the source, and let the ship consume that snapshot. Fire through combat authority/resolver; never apply damage from the pulse mesh or audio callback.
7. **Return/landing:** query one pure landing-assist report from `ShipyardWorld`; show the same report in HUD and request handling; reserve the selected `ShipBerth`; run brake → staging → align → final; revalidate the captured berth/lease/obstruction every step; occupy before snap; emit completion once.
8. **Automatic shutdown/exit:** landing assist retains power through touchdown; once landed, require exactly `1.5` accumulated neutral physics seconds to reach engine offline, with paused/render-only time excluded. Then require landed + occupied + engine offline, run generation-guarded disembark, restore the production capsule at `get_exit_transform()`, clear the seat/active-ship/camera exactly once, and update guided completion only after the physical exit signal.
9. **Recovery/reuse:** on destruction, clear pending landing/boarding/receipts, restore on-foot authority, regenerate only when the home berth can be reserved, and preserve object/connection counts across whole-`Main` detach/re-entry.

**Required tests for any loop change:** start with the affected component test, then add/extend `station_surface_playability_test.gd`, `boarding_accessibility_test.gd`, `controller_physical_sortie_test.gd`, `controller_sortie_lifecycle_test.gd`, `torrent_sortie_completion_test.gd`, `sandbox_loop_test.gd`, `fleet_lifecycle_safety_test.gd`, `main_reentry_quality_test.gd`, and `smoke_test.gd` as applicable. The integration assertion must use the production scene and normal public actions; a test that directly sets the final phase is setup evidence only.

These records began as `CANDIDATE` reports. The recorded audit had
resolved all four code seams below: the receipt collision was reproduced and
fixed; both audio acceptance paths now mutate presentation state only after the
shared playback gate accepts; and the explicit whole-`Main` deferred-damage
discard path was already present and made candidate 4 `NOT_REPRODUCED` on the
current tree. The specifications remain here as regression contracts rather
than work to repeat. Native real-device audibility for items 2 and 3 is still a
release-evidence gap, so a source-level fix must not be mistaken for a heard,
mixed package result.

1. **Combat receipt identity — reproduced and fixed:** `scripts/combat/live_combat_authority.gd` now uses a session-monotonic positive signed-64-bit allocator independent of source ID and request sequence. It begins at `1`, persists on the authority instance, never reuses a session receipt, and fails closed before exhaustion; full source/sequence remain separate in the accepted record. `combat_receipt_identity_test.gd` retains the old signed-shift and `2^32` alias witnesses, source reset/re-registration, saturation, detach/re-entry, and one-target/one-commit gates.
2. **Station cue acceptance — source gate fixed, native listening open:** `scripts/audio/station_machinery_ambience.gd` calls `play()` and requires the real player to report `playing` before success. Rejection stops and detaches the stream and preserves counters/last-cue state; Dummy remains explicitly non-audible. Component invalid/unknown/intensity/teardown/state gates are green, but this host could not open a native output device, so a heard servo/latch pass remains required.
3. **Combat cue acceptance — source gate fixed, native listening open:** the shared `scripts/audio/combat_audio_presentation.gd` playback path updates its pool cursor, counters, last-cue metadata, and `cue_started` only after accepted playback; rejection stops/detaches and leaves the slot available. Focused fire/impact/explosion/dry-fire, overlap, rejection, detach/re-entry and dormant-source gates are green. Dummy simulation remains documented, and native audibility/mix evidence remains open.
4. **Deferred presentation teardown — already landed, current candidate not reproduced:** `GameFlow._exit_tree()` explicitly discards deferred presentation records on all fleet ships, the range opponent, and world targets before clearing coordinator receipts, while standalone `HeroDamagePresentation` still deliberately preserves ordinary detach/re-entry. Focused Main cycles and live-combat teardown prove old hero/opponent/world commits return `false`, every pending queue reaches zero, authoritative health/destruction remains final, and no stale VFX/audio resurrects. No further source change is warranted.

## Phase 3 — Shipyard expansion (bounded operational-lattice slice settled; full phase incomplete)

### Design and implementation specification

- Build each station addition as a bounded module scene with a stable module ID, identity connection anchor, local footprint/AABB, route-marker registry, evidence metadata, semantic component roster, collision/authority/performance report, validation API, and reversible enable/disable lifecycle. World integration owns the global transform and any shared gameplay authority.
- Preserve a single station graph. A module publishes connection planes and route endpoints; `ShipyardWorld` chooses placement and proves adjacency. Do not hide disconnected geometry with teleport triggers, duplicate floors, invisible bridges, or presentation-only shells that imply a route the player cannot walk.
- Separate walkable structure from dressing. Walkable decks, ramps, stairs, shelves, and thresholds use World-layer static collision matched to their visible envelope. Pipes, labels, rails, lamps, trim, machinery covers, and distant shells are collision-free unless they intentionally block the player, and non-walkable horizontal presentation is tagged for discovery audits.
- Keep berth, regeneration, door, activity, and audio ownership external or explicit. A decorative dock marker cannot reserve a ship; a labelled control cannot regenerate one; an activity rail cannot become navigation; an ambience emitter cannot drive a door. New modules consume the existing component APIs instead of creating lookalike local authority.
- Integrate in dependency order: evidence/topology claim → isolated module scene → module audit/test → collision-clear connection transform → production-world route test → nearby berth/ship-envelope regression → Main detach/re-entry → native overview and player-height review.
- Expansion acceptance requires: no changed existing berth transforms/leases unless explicitly scoped; continuous no-jump route from an existing hub; published negative-space samples remain empty; visible floor support discovery stays green; no overlap with landing capture/final hull envelopes; quality-profile budgets are bounded; full core-loop/package gates remain green.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. **Normalize the contract before adding more modules.** Add `scripts/world/station_module_contract.gd` with typed requirements for `get_module_id()`, connection/route specs, local bounds/footprint, evidence metadata, component roster, lifecycle controls, and `get_audit_report()`. Adapt Aft, Habitat, Fleet Dock, and Freight without changing their current behaviour; add `tests/station_module_contract_test.gd` to freeze compatibility.
2. **Add a route registry.** Create `scripts/world/station_route_registry.gd` owned by `ShipyardWorld`. Register module ID + connection plane + route endpoints + evidence status. Reject duplicate IDs, dangling connections, non-finite transforms, missing evidence, overlapping authority IDs, and two modules claiming the same connection slot. Return a deep-copied non-metric adjacency graph for tests/UI only.
3. **Create one module in isolated files:** `scenes/world/modules/<module_id>.tscn`, `scripts/world/<module_id>.gd`, `tests/<module_id>_test.gd`, and optional authored presentation/generator/manifest files. Do not construct the new module procedurally inside `shipyard_world.gd`; that file should instance and place it.
4. **Implement semantic roots first:** `ModuleAnchor`, connection markers, route markers, walkable structure root, presentation root, and deferred/locked landmarks. Then add materials, collision, doors/components, dressing, audio/activity consumers. Every marker gets a stable ID and local transform; every runtime-generated child gets a deterministic name.
5. **Publish local geometry contracts:** exact AABB/footprint, floor elevations, connector width/headroom, critical route samples, negative-space samples, collision layer/mask counts, mesh/light/audio/activity budgets, and prohibited authority node types. Validate all values in `get_audit_report()`.
6. **Integrate through `ShipyardWorld`:** choose one transform from the topology map, connect it to an existing route, register it, and leave existing registered berth transforms unchanged unless the module's explicit feature requires a reviewed berth migration. Run overlap queries against every assist-capture/final hull envelope and neighbouring ship collision.
7. **Prove real traversal:** extend `station_surface_playability_test.gd` with start/end transforms and continuous production input; extend `station_interaction_flow_test.gd` for doors/controls; add module-specific route/occupancy/negative-space assertions. No teleport is allowed between the connection threshold and destination.
8. **Add richer station life only through reusable data:** extend `StationOperationsActivity` profiles first. If agents need free routing, then add `station_navigation_graph.gd` and `station_service_agent.gd` with stable IDs, bounded service envelopes, pause/disable/reset/re-entry methods, deterministic seeds, and no berth/combat/regeneration authority.
9. **Review and release:** run 30/60/120 Hz activity equivalence, teardown/re-entry identity/count checks, station collision/material discovery, full-fleet berth lifecycle tests, native overview plus player-height connection/interior frames, full matrix, package smoke, and human walk-through.

## Phase 4 — Original fleet

### Design and implementation specification

- Implement one evidence-bounded craft at a time through the same pipeline: ledger/evidence spec → removable source-core design → editable Blender source and deterministic generator where used → GLB plus manifest → presentation wrapper/audit → `ShipDefinition` → ship scene/physics → boarding/seat/camera/muzzle/damage anchors → collision proposal → berth integration → focused lifecycle and native captures.
- Keep three contracts separate: **historical evidence** describes what may be claimed, **presentation art** describes what is rendered, and **gameplay collision/handling** describes modern playable normalization. Runtime collision must never be loaded from an editable manifest as authority; consume reviewed, pinned geometry/constants and compare them back to the non-authoritative art proposal.
- Collision acceptance is bidirectional. Every solid art vertex must be within the allowed collision coverage tolerance, and exposed collision boundary samples must remain close enough to visible solid art to avoid invisible blockers. Test the exact production player capsule along the boarding route, all berth-fit corners, muzzle clearance, landing obstruction, parked-neighbour separation, and moving-interior boundaries.
- LODs switch atomically by semantic layer, preserve material/anchor identities, and contain no scripts, collision, cameras, audio, navigation, animation authority, or gameplay metadata inside imported art. Hiding modern systems must leave the documented source-supported silhouette legible.
- A ship is accepted only after normal walk-up/boarding, same-tick automatic demand, launch, handling, firing, damage/destruction/recovery, broad assist acquisition, strict landing, automatic neutral shutdown, exit, craft switching, and whole-Main re-entry all pass in production. Neutral source-vs-current views may support bounded recognition, but tests/renders do not upgrade historical authentication.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. **Choose evidence status first.** For an original-labelled craft, update the dated source ledger/matrix and write `docs/<CRAFT>_RECONSTRUCTION_SPEC.md`. If there is no continuous name-to-model chain, implement only as a clearly provisional candidate or do not implement the silhouette yet.
2. **Preserve roster variants.** Add `docs/research/fleet_roster_variants.json` keyed by source/version scope and validate unique IDs/evidence links from `research_evidence_test.gd`. Keep the frozen four-craft vertical-slice roster named and stable while a distinct current runtime roster and separate dated/full evidence roster grow.
3. **Create the asset package:** `tools/blender/generate_<craft>_v1.py` when deterministic generation is used, `art_source/<craft>/<craft>_v1.blend`, `assets/models/<craft>/<craft>_art.glb`, manifest/import sidecar, `scenes/ships/presentation/<craft>_presentation.tscn`, wrapper script, and focused authored-asset test. Regeneration must preserve declared hashes or explain deterministic source changes.
4. **Structure the import:** one exact art root; `SourceCore/LOD0` and `SourceCore/LOD1`; separately tagged `ModernSystems/LOD0`, `ModernSystems/LOD1`, and semantic anchors. The wrapper resolves anchors by stable names, applies registered materials, performs atomic LOD switching, exposes deep-copy audit reports, and rejects extra visual/authority siblings.
5. **Define gameplay data:** add `assets/ships/<craft>.tres` using `ShipDefinition` and a ship subclass/scene under `scripts/ships/` and `scenes/ships/`. Fill identity/evidence references, compatibility tags, flight/system profile, entry copy, and audio profile. Add only schema fields shared by multiple craft; subclass-only constants remain in the subclass with validation.
6. **Pin semantic anchors:** boarding point/entry, exit, pilot seat, cockpit camera, muzzle(s), damage centre/zones, docking receiver/contact, engine plumes, and any passenger/interior frames. Test exact transforms against the wrapper and verify they remain reachable/clear in the complete scene.
7. **Design collision from art, then hard-code reviewed authority:** generate a non-authoritative collision proposal; decompose concave forms; measure art→collision coverage and exposed collision→art overreach; test player capsule boarding sweep, muzzle rays, landing bounds, neighbour clearance, and all visible solid exclusions. Runtime code uses reviewed constants/resources, not live manifest bytes.
8. **Integrate only after isolated lifecycle passes:** asset audit, ship definition, boarding, seated camera, automatic engine demand/idle plus internal start/stop API compatibility, command/flight, fire/damage/destruction/reset, landing clearance, and detach/re-entry. Then add a world berth/feedback/access route, update exact fleet/source/audio/berth rosters, and run a normal-input production sortie.
9. **Review evidence and playability separately:** neutral source-bounded views judge the documented macroform; native gameplay views judge readability/access/contact. A green comparison cannot change `provisional`/`bounded_partial` to `authenticated`.

## Phase 5 — Expanded fleet

### Design and implementation specification

- Document the shared visual grammar before adding craft: silhouette families, scale bands, material/value hierarchy, cockpit/access conventions, engine-language boundaries, colour readability, damage anchors, and evidence status. New craft may vary the grammar deliberately but must not become unlabelled substitutes for unknown originals.
- Add roles through data-driven `ShipDefinition` resources and existing `HeroShip`-compatible authority seams. A new ship supplies handling, collision, boarding/seat/camera/muzzle/damage anchors, audio profile, compatibility tags, and presentation; it does not fork GameFlow, landing, combat resolution, or lifecycle logic unless the role proves a missing reusable capability.
- Balance laterally with a written trade-off table: acceleration, top speed, rotational response, braking, toughness, weapon envelope, crew/cargo utility, landing footprint, and access time. No craft should dominate every axis, and starter fighters remain immediately usable.
- Each fleet increment includes one craft and its required berth/access changes only. Acceptance repeats the Phase 4 physical lifecycle, adds cross-craft switching and neighbour-clearance tests, updates exact fleet/berth/source/audio rosters, and restores the packaged playable-prototype gate before another craft begins.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. `docs/design/FLEET_VISUAL_GRAMMAR.md` now exists and is derived from the original four-craft vertical slice; Halyard is the fifth craft assessed against it. It records silhouette and proportion language, the two-layer body/accent colour system and its frozen CIEDE2000 separation floors, per-craft material and surface treatment, scale-to-role gates, cockpit and boarding conventions, what is evidence-bounded versus free, an explicit "what a new craft must not do" section, and the operational lateral-trade-off rule. Extend and correct it rather than rewriting it, and keep it green: `tests/fleet_visual_grammar_doc_test.gd` fails when a documented floor, surface value, or evidence status stops matching the constant, source file, or ledger row that owns it. Anything the document still leaves open — audio grammar, LOD targets, damage/debris presentation — is listed in its own final section.
2. Create a role matrix covering mobility, rotational response, braking, durability, firepower/range, cargo/passenger/support utility, footprint, boarding time, and skill floor. Give every craft a weakness and an intended player story. Add a normalized role-budget resource/test so no same-band ship is a strict upgrade.
3. Use `ShipDefinition.EvidenceStatus.NEW` for new ships; do not attach historical evidence as authentication. Reuse the Phase 4 asset/presentation/collision pipeline and the existing `HeroShip`, `ShipCommand`, `ShipBerth`, `ShipBoardingArea`, `ShipAudioRig`, damage, landing, and reuse contracts.
4. If the role needs a new reusable capability—cargo authority, turret seats, bomber payloads, repair, crew stations—implement and test that capability as its own typed component before the ship consumes it. Do not bury the system in one subclass.
5. For larger interiors, use `MovingInteriorFrame`, publish floor/seat/exit markers, keep passenger collision stable through flight, and test entry/exit velocity transfer, destruction, landing, and detach/re-entry. Decorative passenger space is not multi-crew gameplay until roles and authority exist.
6. Integrate exactly one new craft, its compatible berth/access route, definition/audio profile, and any required UI copy. Update fleet roster tests without weakening the frozen four-craft vertical-slice roster; test old and expanded rosters explicitly.
7. Run isolated lifecycle, shared-world neighbour clearance, all-craft boarding/switching, handling comparison, combat/landing/recovery, performance budget, native visual/audio, and human balance passes before starting the next role.

## Phase 6 — Expanded combat and damage

### Design and implementation specification

- Preserve the authority chain: `ShipCommand` requests fire → combat authority validates source/cadence → `CombatResolver` resolves world occlusion/faction/endpoint → damage adapter changes authoritative health/collision/score once → pooled presentation/audio consume the accepted receipt. No mesh, particle, sound, or camera effect performs a second ray query or applies damage.
- Define weapons as immutable profiles with faction policy, cadence, range, damage, spread/aim rule, heat/ammunition if used, and presentation/audio IDs. Projectiles that need travel-time gameplay become server-ready authority objects; hitscan weapons remain resolved immediately with delayed presentation only.
- Build one shared damage-state model before multiplying effects: health thresholds, component states, power/handling consequences, repair/reset rules, destruction sequence, debris authority, respawn/regeneration, and generation-safe cleanup. Hero ships, range opponents, and targets should adapt to it rather than retain divergent visual lifecycles.
- Pool transients and set explicit budgets for simultaneous shots, lights, particles, debris, audio voices, nodes, materials, and lifetimes. World-space effects capture the accepted impact/destruction pose and must not follow a moved, hidden, detached, or recycled owner.
- Acceptance includes miss/occlusion/friendly/self cases, reverse-order receipt arrival, saturation/recycle/abort re-entrancy, lethal and non-lethal audio chronology, destruction during detach/re-entry, reset/regeneration, no duplicate score/damage, native legibility at combat range with glow disabled and enabled, and restored full packaged loop.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. Add `scripts/combat/weapon_definition.gd` as a validated `Resource` with stable weapon ID, resolution mode, range, damage, cadence, faction/friendly-fire policy, optional spread/heat/ammunition fields, and presentation/audio IDs. First migrate current constants into resources with byte/behaviour-equivalent tests; do not change balance during migration.
2. Make `LiveCombatAuthority` validate source ownership, sequence, finite origin/direction, cadence, weapon ID, and current lifecycle before constructing a `ShotRequest`. Make `CombatResolver` the only world ray/occlusion/faction/endpoint decision for hitscan.
3. Add one typed damage contract (`damage_component.gd` / `component_damage_model.gd`) with stable component IDs, maximum/current health, stage thresholds, gameplay consequences, signals, `apply_component_damage(context)`, `get_component_state(id)`, and `reset_for_reuse()`. Adapt existing hull damage without changing outcomes before adding engines/weapons/controls failures.
4. Add `repair_authority.gd` only after component damage is stable. Validate actor, range/seat, resource/cooldown, damaged component, generation, and interruption; commit repair once; keep tool animation/audio presentation-only.
5. Route accepted result in this order: authoritative hull/component state and collision/score → create bounded deferred presentation record → launch/recycle pooled pulse → commit impact/explosion/audio at receipt arrival or abort fallback → erase coordinator metadata. Store accepted world pose/velocity, never resample a recycled owner.
6. Add a new weapon/opponent as one scenario: definition, authority validation, resolver case, damage consequence, pooled visuals/audio, AI use if relevant, UI feedback, and cleanup. Do not add multiple weapons before the first restores the complete core loop.
7. Test duplicates/out-of-order sequences, invalid owner/faction, self/friendly/world occlusion, miss, close/min-duration hit, hitch past impact, saturation/reentrant callbacks, reverse receipt arrival, lethal/nonlethal chronology, detach/re-entry, reset/regeneration, repair interruption, exact pool/resource ceilings, and one score/damage commit.
8. Capture phase-locked muzzle, mid-flight, impact, damaged, critical, explosion, and cleanup frames at combat distance with High and glow-disabled profiles. Human review must confirm colour/team distinction, endpoint alignment, effect size, damage readability, no hard pop, and acceptable audio chronology/mix.

## Phase 7 — Multiplayer

### Design and implementation specification

- Do not network the current single-player `GameFlow` as one replicated global state. Introduce a server-owned session/world coordinator, per-peer avatar/seat state, stable network entity IDs, and explicit replicated snapshots while retaining the production Player, ship, berth, boarding, command, combat, damage, and moving-interior components behind server/replica modes.
- Prove the first slice with three real OS processes: one authoritative headless ENet server and two clients loading the same bounded station/Jovian scene. Both clients can walk; client A atomically claims the pilot seat; client B claims a stable passenger seat; only A's validated `ShipCommand` controls the craft; B remains seated through flight; both disembark coherently.
- The server alone owns movement truth, boarding/seat reservations, ship simulation, combat resolution, damage, landing leases, occupancy, destruction, and respawn. Clients send rate-limited intent with sequence/tick numbers, predict only explicitly allowed local presentation, interpolate remote snapshots, and reconcile without changing authority.
- Replicate moving-interior relationships in frame-local coordinates with generation IDs. Test packet loss, jitter, latency, reordering, disconnect while seated/piloting/landing, ownership transfer, late join, destroyed-owner cleanup, and malicious invalid commands before raising player count.
- Multiplayer acceptance requires deterministic loopback integration, no duplicate entities or seats across re-entry, bounded bandwidth/tick budgets, clear ownership UI, a native-Windows two-client playtest, and the complete solo playable gate still green.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. Create `scripts/network/network_session_coordinator.gd` for host/join/shutdown and peer lifecycle, `network_entity_registry.gd` for stable network ID + generation ↔ node mapping, `remote_ship_command_source.gd` for server-side command validation, `network_snapshot.gd` for typed state, and `network_seat_authority.gd` for atomic seat claims. Keep RPC entry points in this layer instead of scattering them through Player/ship/GameFlow scripts.
2. Session API: `host(port, max_peers)`, `join(address, port)`, `shutdown(reason)`, peer-connected/disconnected signals, and a deep-copy audit. Registry API: `register_entity(id, generation, node)`, `resolve(id, generation)`, `retire(id, generation)`, with duplicate/stale-generation rejection and cleanup on tree exit.
3. Client command packet fields: peer ID, controlled entity ID/generation, stream ID, monotonic sequence, client tick, and serialized `ShipCommand`. Server validates current pilot-seat ownership, allowed tick window/rate, unique stream/sequence, finite/clamped axes, edge-action rules, and lifecycle before exposing one command to the authoritative ship.
4. Snapshot fields: server tick, entity ID/generation, parent frame ID/generation, frame-local/global transform as applicable, linear/angular velocity, engine/landed/damage state, seat assignments, and authoritative event sequence. Replicas interpolate presentation only and cannot call engine, damage, landing, berth, boarding, score, or regeneration setters.
5. First network scene contains the bounded station, production Player replicas, and Jovian. Launch one headless server and two client OS processes: both walk; A and B race for seats; one pilot claim wins; B occupies a passenger seat; only A flies; B remains stable in the moving interior; server lands; both exit.

Add `tests/network/` unit/component cases plus a three-process harness covering host/join, spoofed owner, duplicate/out-of-order commands, simultaneous seat/berth claims, 100 ms RTT + 2% loss/jitter/reorder, disconnect during boarding/flight/landing, late join/resync, ownership transfer, destruction/respawn, and entity cleanup. Dedicated server must run without render/audio authority.
7. Require a 30-minute two-client soak with zero authority divergence, duplicate entities/seats, unbounded queue growth, or leaks; record tick/bandwidth budgets and complete a native-Windows two-client playtest before increasing player count or implementing gunner/engineer roles.
