Deterministic jitter/reorder/teleport/lifecycle/budget tests and the exact three-process 100 ms RTT/loss harness are green, but the 30-minute soak and native Windows two-client review are still missing, so this remains open. **Partially closed 2026-09-15:** `tests/network_moving_interior_latency_test.gd` runs the real ENet session on loopback (server on production Main with the Halyard's moving frame, two clients) through a test-only transport hook that delays, jitters, reorders and drops relationship packets, across clean / 80 ms±20 / 200 ms±60 / 350 ms±120+2 % loss / 1.5 s stall while a client walks the cabin, sleeps in a bunk, transfers seats, drops and reconnects, and the server re-enters Main: frame-local reconstruction exact, extrapolation pinned at the 0.675 m horizon, every pose inside the live frame, 0 teleports across 874 re-ordered arrivals, generations never regress. Four defects fixed: a delivery gap wider than the jitter window froze a crewmate permanently (now a counted re-baseline), a disconnected crewmate stayed on screen as a phantom (explicit release broadcast), `shutdown()` left replica state behind for the reconnect, and replica sample history nested without bound (1,001 recursion errors in 570 ticks). **Then (8cbc58458):** `NetworkMovingInteriorPresenter` draws one production pilot avatar per tracked relationship on client peers, sampled every rendered frame and composed with the live moving frame, removed on release/disconnect/migration/re-entry; the replica timeline is converted to seconds at the single arrival seam (horizon still 0.675 m); two more defects fixed (the replica binding refused every production frame because craft are `CharacterBody3D`, and a published release never retired the authority's own occupancy). **Then (2f86f2799):** the authority publishes every identified occupant of every moving interior each server tick with live frame-local pose, `occupancy_state` (walking/seated/sleeping, schema 2) and locomotion hint; secured occupancies go out at a critical priority so coalescing never parks a seat pose (measured worst lag 1 tick vs 8 for a walker); one relationship per occupant across sit→walk→sleep→wake→disembark; two more defects fixed (a released crewmate resurrected by their own withheld snapshot, an inactive peer asked for an authority answer). **Then (71b3047ef):** GameFlow owns exactly one session adapter at the canonical `NetworkSession` path and retires it with the subtree that owns it (shutdown while the RPC path is live, unbind the shared signal table, synchronous remove, free), so hosting or joining after a whole-Main re-entry works — seat claim, cabin publication and a projectile round-trip all through one adapter — and a stopped session restores the offline multiplayer peer instead of leaving every per-frame peer-id query erroring (40 engine errors per re-entry window before). **Remote bodies simulated, 2026-09-15 (02aafbbf3 → 1e4309e48):** the movement intent contract is schema 2 (look yaw/pitch, run/crouch/jump, monotonic interaction request; schema 1 still admitted) on the one existing movement RPC and ledger; a client `NetworkRemoteBodyIntentSource` streams at 15 Hz with jump/interact edge latching, and on the authority `NetworkRemoteBodySimulation` instantiates the production `player.tscn` per admitted remote occupant — same capsule, floor snap, step-up, cabin containment and seat transitions — registered with the craft's `MovingInteriorFrame` and driven only by intent the ledger accepted (`not_avatar_owner`, `spoofed_peer`, `stale_avatar_generation`, `stale_sequence` refused before anything reaches a body; silence > 12 ticks freezes it). Seat and bunk requests resolve against what the *server* body's interaction area actually overlaps, through production `StationSeat` reserve → board → disembark → release, so the publisher now reports simulated poses and states to every peer including the owner; bodies exist only while an occupant does (resident census unchanged) and are released on peer loss, session stop, craft loss and whole-Main detach. The owning client predicts with its own `PlayerController` and snaps on > 0.5 m disagreement (no input replay by design). Three further defects fixed on the way: a coalesced walker froze permanently on every client once the seated pilot's critical snapshot filled the window (the relationship stream now resumes on the first ordered packet), every intent was swallowed by the remote ship-command source whenever any remote pilot existed, and an engine error per send across a reconnect. A 115-assertion ENet suite drives a remote walker down a flying Halyard aisle with collision, seat sit/stand, forged/stale intent rejection and re-host after re-entry. **Crowd budget measured** (1 pilot + N walkers, 5 recipients, `docs/MOVING_INTERIOR_LATENCY.md`): snapshots/tick 2.0 / 3.0 / 5.0 for N = 1 / 2 / 4 with exact reconstruction in every row; worst pose lag is set by the window roll (sub-metre for N ≤ 2, 4.2 m once for N = 4 on a gap-hold) — the next headroom is not sending a critical snapshot for a secured occupant every tick. **Follow-up 2026-09-15 (cad66a0ad, bd657d4ce, 82f4e42b5):** a seated or sleeping remote body is put into the ledger's `seated` mode, so walking intent is refused by name (`movement_while_seated`, counted in the authority audit) and accepted again on standing; a boarding confirmed through the hatch on a craft with a walkable interior stands a body at the cabin stand pose (the server registers every such craft with the boarding ledger: pilot seat plus four cabin berths) and a networked disembark releases it, proven end to end over ENet; and a secured occupant's pose is published at critical priority once on the transition and then re-stated every 8 ticks (the jitter buffer's gap bound) instead of every tick, with secured relationships never gap-held, so walkers stop being parked until the window roll — snapshots/tick fell from 1+N to N+0.13 and the N = 4 clean worst pose lag from 4.16 m to 0.97 m (outside the measured run-to-run variance; N ≤ 2 differences are within it; both tables in the doc). **Client seam closed 2026-09-20 (the eight commits ending 18bef7f6e):** the production hatch on a network client now sends a boarding intent instead of boarding locally — a cabin berth for a walkable-interior craft, the pilot seat otherwise — and the host answers the requesting peer over one new server→client RPC on the same canonical adapter, carrying the verdict, the request identity, the migration generation and the ledger tick. A confirmed berth is presented through the very seam a locally boarded player uses and then bound so the server body is driven and the local prediction corrected; a disembark releases nothing until confirmed; a refusal renders the ledger's own reason on the existing card; `seat_occupied` walks to the next berth rather than failing; and a four-second timeout, a dead session or a host that stops answering leaves the player standing exactly where they were. A new 45-assertion suite runs two whole production `Main` subtrees plus three berth-holding adapters in one process to prove the press, the walk, the confirmed release, the full-ledger refusal and the timeout. An adversarial review of the author's own change found and fixed seven holes before merge, including a permanent boarding lockout when a grant arrived for an abandoned request, an expiry clock that froze during an expedition, and answer revisions that a host migration would have muted for the rest of the session. **Still open:** a networked passenger cannot be promoted to pilot in place (the ledger has no atomic seat swap), a full craft costs four round trips to discover it is full, the ledger's tick handshake is inert because nothing sets a server tick yet, the two-`GameFlow` proof shares one engine and one input singleton rather than being two processes, the 8-snapshots/10-tick ceiling is still the crowd's floor at N ≥ 2, and the ledger holds no occupancy for the host's own seat.

## Phase 8 — Nearby world and activities

### Design and implementation specification

- Build a small authored activity cluster around the shipyard, not a generated galaxy. Establish one world-coordinate/streaming contract, a maximum travel-time envelope from the station, fixed navigation landmarks, and explicit return routes before adding destinations.
- Implement one activity end to end at a time—destination geometry/collision, approach cues, objective authority, failure/recovery, reward/state reset, audio/presentation, save/session implications, and return to the same occupied shipyard—using reusable activity definitions rather than objective logic embedded in scenery.
- Preserve the station as the visual and logistical anchor. Large coloured bodies and landmarks provide orientation; beacons/races/patrols/cargo/convoys/defence reuse command, combat, damage, cargo, and session seams instead of spawning parallel mechanics.
- Acceptance measures uninterrupted travel and return, no floating-origin or precision instability, bounded active/rendered/physics/audio budgets, deterministic reset/re-entry, no stranded ships or objectives, readable navigation without debug markers, and completion in the packaged build.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. Add `WorldLocationDefinition` resources under `assets/world/` with stable ID, scene path, transform/bounds, landmark/navigation data, evidence/design status, and per-profile budgets. Add `ActivityDefinition` resources under `assets/activities/` with activity ID/type, start/finish volumes, prerequisites, ordered objective IDs, failure/reset/reward rules, and compatible ship/cargo tags.
2. Add `scripts/world/world_streaming_coordinator.gd` with `register_location()`, `request_load()`, `request_unload()`, `get_loaded_ids()`, generation-safe callbacks, and audit. Add `scripts/activities/activity_director.gd` with `can_start()`, `start()`, `get_state()`, `fail()`, `complete()`, and `reset(generation)`. Scenery exposes markers/volumes but never grants rewards or mutates objectives.
3. Create a hand-authored `scenes/world/nearby_sector.tscn` with one navigation beacon/out-and-back route first. Prove load, travel, landmark readability, return, unload/re-entry, world-coordinate precision, and performance before adding an objective.
4. Implement activities in order: checkpoint race → cargo delivery → patrol → convoy/defence. Each adds definition, authority/objective component, HUD signal consumer, failure/recovery, reset, tests, and one packaged human route. Do not add cargo delivery until a typed inventory/transfer authority exists; entering a decorative volume is not proof of cargo delivery.
5. Keep `GameFlow` from accumulating one phase enum branch per activity. It requests the `ActivityDirector`, observes objective/activity signals, and returns to the same general free-flight/shipyard lifecycle. Multiplayer sessions, when present, make the server director authoritative.
6. Test duplicate/invalid IDs, unreachable waypoints, wrong craft/cargo, abort/retry, destruction/recovery, completion exactly once, ten same-world repeats without state growth, save/session restoration, location generation/re-entry, and station→destination→same-ship return. Run active/render/physics/audio budget and no-debug packaged navigation review.

- [ ] Add a concentrated cluster of colourful planets/moons, asteroid and debris fields, abandoned structures, mining platforms, navigation beacons, races, patrols, cargo runs, convoys, and station defence. **First destination you can go inside, 2026-09-20 (1b2f803cd, a4b233f35):** everything in the nearby sector was something to fly past or scan; there is now an 80 m abandoned service-station hulk 486 m out, lying across the approach with a lit dock shelf on its station-facing flank. The player parks on an ordinary berth lease, shuts down, climbs out onto the shelf and walks in through the hull aperture to three connected emergency-lit spaces on real collision — dock vestibule, spine corridor, reactor gallery — where throwing the auxiliary breaker restores the bus and grants one salvaged power cell, exactly once, surviving a save, a whole-Main re-entry and the trip home. No parallel systems were invented: the dock is a plain `ShipBerth` reached through one new resolver that answers from the resident registry first and the streamed berth second, so reservation, landing assist, departure and release stay on the existing path, and the reward rides the existing adapter and reward authority. It costs the resident scene nothing because the sector streams; one loaded Cinder generation gains 5,448 triangles, 39 renderers, 8 shadowless practicals and 92 nodes. One real defect surfaced and was fixed: the streamed transition presentation fails *visually closed* on an unrecognised renderer roster, so adding content without refreezing it hid the whole generation. Not claimed: no rendered or human review of the approach silhouette, and the activity is reached by walking to the breaker rather than from the Activity Board. **Asteroid belt, 2026-09-20 (e9d9dda86, 496221511):** the sector had a debris field of fragments to fly past but nothing with mass to fly *through*; there is now a 295 m belt of thirty 22–50 m rocks with real collision starboard of the outbound route, carrying a 44 m cyan-chevroned bore along its whole length so a player who wants nothing to do with it holds the lane at cruise and touches nothing. Taking the threading run pulls you out of the bore and back across it through five amber gates with roughly 35 m gaps, and clipping a rock stops the hull dead and ends the run. It reuses the existing checkpoint-route activity type behind its own director and definition rather than inventing one, and its reward rides the existing ledger. Placement was checked against every published lane first — the beacon corridor and its four keep-clears, the platform approach, the moonlet, the hulk and the four convoy legs — and the placement code re-runs those predicates per candidate so a later nudge fails loudly. Loaded Cinder gains 13,824 triangles, 8 renderers and 72 nodes with no new light of any kind; the resident scene is untouched. The streamed transition rosters were refrozen as the hulk pass warned, and the belt's own suite now asserts that roster so a future renderer fails a belt test instead of silently hiding the sector. Not claimed: no rendered look-check of chevron readability or rock tint, and a player who ignores the HUD objective may not realise the belt is enterable — the sector is now legible from the cockpit instead. **Sector legibility, 2026-09-20 (3d142dc5e → 172b2c9b1):** the hulk's dock face, the belt's bore mouth, the four route beacons, the ringed moonlet, the extraction platform and the debris field all carry minimap marks with their own glyph, pattern and label, drawn only while the sector is streamed in and the player is in the seat. Coming within 250 m of the hulk's dock or the belt's mouth fires one briefing on the existing tutorial-card channel telling the player what it is and which control engages it, once each and remembered across a re-entry. The Destination Board lists the hulk and the bore beside Ember as a separate site roster, so the world count and the console's own line are unchanged, and a site is offered only on a well-typed residency report — while the sector is away or the player is on foot both rows read `OUT OF SENSOR RANGE` and are disabled, with the handler re-checking residency rather than trusting the button. Colour carries nothing on its own (shape and text per family, checked under a flat single-hue palette) and no marker blinks or pulses. The only census movement is +18 nodes resident and loaded, exactly the board's two retained pause-menu cards at nine Controls each, with every geometry row byte-identical.
- [ ] Keep the shipyard the social and logistical heart; do not expand into a procedural galaxy.

### Delivered so far — the Cinder Reach cluster (`scripts/world/nearby_sector_cluster.gd`)

The first typed activity authority now composes the existing Cinder Reach checkpoint route: `TimedCheckpointRace` owns caller-physics-delta countdown/race timing, ordered multi-lap progress, penalties, timeout/failure/reset, generation rejection, and best/current/last results. The reusable authority itself deliberately adds no geometry, rewards, HUD, `GameFlow`, ship, combat, berth, or network integration; production composition is the separate session layer below.

A `CinderTimedRaceSession` now joins that timer to `ActivityDirector`: the existing director alone accepts world positions and the existing route resource alone owns checkpoint geometry, while the session maps their independent generations, rolls the director route between configured laps, and publishes detached presentation snapshots. The first production integration is live in `GameFlow`: general free flight starts one lap with a two-second physics countdown and 120-second timeout, samples only the active production ship's world position once per piloted physics tick, and presents countdown/lap/gate/current/best/failure state through the HUD. Whole-`Main` detach/re-entry retains one session/director identity without advancing time or duplicating samples. The session itself still grants no reward and owns no ship, berth, combat, world, or network authority; its authenticated terminal snapshot now crosses GameFlow's separate generation fence into one persisted, non-replayable Shipyard race-record receipt (`tests/cinder_activity_integration_test.gd`, 39 assertions). Packaged route completion and human flight review remain open.

The next typed activity is `PatrolActivity`: it reuses that exact Cinder beacon route as one honest inspection sweep, reads its existing volumes for caller-physics continuous dwell, and lets `ActivityDirector` commit each ordered checkpoint only after dwell. Production `GameFlow` now owns one lifetime-stable patrol adapter beside the timed-race adapter, attaches exactly one of them to the shared route, samples the active ship once per patrol physics tick, and presents travel/dwell/completion/failure/abort through the HUD. Selection locks on the first accepted start, destruction fails the current generation, return aborts it, and whole-`Main` detach/re-entry preserves partial dwell and identity. A completed, failed, or aborted generation remains terminal through ticks and whole-`Main` re-entry; the selected Activity Board action then advertises `REPEAT` and crosses the existing generation-fenced reset seam before admitting exactly one fresh start with cleared dwell/progress and no duplicate samples or signals. The pause-menu Activity Board exposes Timed Race, Patrol, Jovian Kit Delivery, and Emberline Convoy Escort through real focusable HUD controls; rejected replacement rolls back atomically and the choice locks after an accepted start. During a live race or patrol, the minimap now observes the selected adapter's current generation and the shared `ActivityDirector` definition to display the next authored route gate with a distinct non-colour glyph and distance; terminal state removes that marker without retaining a stale target. The streamed activity binding uses the same presentation boundary for nearby tasks: debris traversal publishes each already-authoritative next beacon, while mining and structure scan publish their exact active hold points; each uses a distinct non-colour glyph and disappears on completion, interruption, reset, or unload. Selecting the Emberline convoy now adds its audited rendezvous to the minimap, then switches to the retained host's world-space next-leg target during escort and withdraws both phases on any terminal state. The Cinder platform-supply run now guides its live load, physical clear-gate, and return phases from the existing berth/capture geometry, then withdraws the target before terminal handoff. An active Jovian fabrication-kit delivery observes ShipyardWorld's physical freight-berth transform during its return phase and removes that destination immediately after landing, failure, or expiry. The compact map draws legend rows only for objectives present in its current snapshot instead of listing every possible task. Patrol still adds no geometry, ship, combat, berth, save, or network authority of its own; an authenticated completion now produces one separate persisted Shipyard patrol-log receipt. The physical station Activity Board is also production-wired: the Aft Operations console opens the existing focused HUD page and mirrors persisted receipt summaries through GameFlow (`tests/station_interaction_flow_test.gd`, `tests/cinder_activity_integration_test.gd`). It now offers Relay Sweep and Platform Sweep before start; the chosen order locks for the generation, persists across detach and fresh-process restore, drives only its own next-gate guidance, and records one branch-specific receipt through the existing reward authority (`tests/patrol_production_integration_test.gd`, 41 assertions). Packaged human flight review remains open.

The standalone `ConvoyEscortActivity` foundation now snapshots ordered legs from an `ActivityDirector` definition, binds one protected convoy identity/generation, accepts caller-owned convoy/escort position and status samples, and owns proximity/separation, physics-only timeout, safe-arrival/destroyed/lost/abort/reset results, generation rejection, signal re-entry guards, and detached HUD-ready state. `CinderConvoyEscortHost` now supplies one explicit NEW/`modern_interpretation` Emberline tender and four-leg route, moves it at caller-physics speed, publishes exact entity samples, and proves arrival, separation grace, telemetry loss, reset, and detach/re-entry over that authority (`tests/cinder_convoy_escort_host_test.gd`, 23 assertions). The reusable host itself deliberately does not apply combat or damage, grant rewards, transfer cargo, select ships/berths, drive GameFlow/HUD, save, network, or choose production placement; the production composition below observes it without moving those authorities into the host.

The production composition now places exactly one identity `CinderConvoyEscortHost` under `Main`, never under the streamed Cinder scene, and exposes **Emberline Convoy Escort** as the fourth real Activity Board choice. A sortie starts only from the audited 4 m rendezvous sphere centred at `(84, -48, -724)` — the collision-clear player lane 20 m above the tender's unchanged route — with the current Cinder generation loaded, the selected healthy ship piloted, physically departed, and in free flight. One captured ship position feeds both the streaming policy and escort authority per physics tick. Stream unload/replacement, ship replacement, unpiloting, destruction/recovery, or landing fail the exact active generation before adjacent lifecycle work can diverge; whole-`Main` detach/re-entry retains one host/activity identity. Safe arrival now retires the live convoy session before committing one separate, non-replayable Shipyard escort-credit receipt; the host still grants no berth, cargo, combat, save, or network authority.

**Emberline defence, 2026-09-26:** a red raider now follows the moving tender within the authored route, fires through the existing `LiveCombatAuthority` and `CombatResolver`, and can destroy its damageable hull before arrival. The player can shoot and neutralize the raider with an existing ship weapon. The raider is currently a clear emissive box; native rendered appearance and normal-controls human flight review are still open.

The **destination** half of the first item exists. Flying out of the launch corridor now reaches a place: a four-beacon route chain from 241 m to 603 m, a solid ringed moonlet 619 m to port, a sixteen-boulder debris drift with a 720-instance debris shell, an open 28 x 23 m dock gate on the platform's approach lane, and the derelict Cinder Reach extraction platform 706 m out — roughly nine seconds outbound at Torrent cruise, six on boost. Every position is a named constant and there is no generator. The component is no longer always resident: production streams the authored scene as one coordinator-owned generation at its zero scene origin while distance policy reads the separately registered Cinder navigation anchor. Nothing the component builds comes nearer than 200 m to the station or reaches past 900 m, so the launch corridor, the target range and the landing approach are untouched and the backdrop star shell at 1450 m stays where it was.

It owns **no gameplay authority**: no rewards, no leases, no objectives, and deliberately no range targets, because the guided mission's objective count is `ShipyardWorld.get_target_count()`. Its solid bodies sit on the same World collision layer the station uses, so the existing `HeroShip` hull-impact path is the only damage route involved. Regression: `tests/nearby_sector_cluster_test.gd` (68 assertions; frozen placement contract, approach-lane and keep-clear scatter scan, outward-winding scan over the built tree, collision-layer boundary, seed determinism, detach/re-entry lifecycle). Rendered and flown evidence: `tests/nearby_sector_flight_review.gd`.

**The outbound route out of the launch corridor is now clear of the range gate — fixed 2026-08-16.** The review flight that produced the evidence above flew the production Torrent into the target range's own header beam at **46 m/s** on its first run, 51 m past the launch gate, and recorded it rather than moving the map. Two things were wrong, and neither of them was the range:

- The station's own published outbound aim, the `LaunchGate` marker, sat at **y = 8.0**, which is *inside* the band that beam blocks. Measured against the real production hulls on the launch centreline, as ship-origin altitude: a Torrent holding altitude out of the corridor is stopped by `RangeHeader` for every altitude from **4.8 to 10.2 m**, and the marker pointed at the middle of it. The aperture is the same height right across the gate's 63 m — every sampled x from −30 to +30 gives the same 4.70 m ceiling — so there is no lateral way round it, and over the top needs y ≥ 10.3 (Torrent) or 10.8 (Jovian), an 8 m climb inside the 56 m available. **Under is the only line all nine flyables can take**, which is the line the Cinder Reach beacon chain was already drawn for: `RouteBeaconAlpha` is at y = −9. The original five-craft repair moved the marker `(0, 8, -64) -> (0, 2.5, -64)`; the nine-craft integration rerun found that its published **1.24 m** floor omitted the Cinder bomber's measured **1.60 m** corridor floor and left that craft only 0.90 m below the aim. The marker is now at `(0, 2.7, -64)`, the centre of the independently fleet-worst **1.60 – 3.80 m** band (Cinder bomber floor / Jovian ceiling), and `ShipyardWorld.get_outbound_clearance_band()` keeps the marker, flight review and regression on that same measured envelope. The complete route sweep now runs every production hull rather than three selected historical extremes.
- **The beam did not read as an obstacle.** Over its whole 63 m it carried no lamp, no marking and no legend; the gate's only lamps were six on the trusses, 31 m off the centreline and *above* the beam. The rendered before/after (`artifacts/range-gate/`, `tests/capture_range_gate_clearance.gd`, each shot twice from the same camera with the cue shown and hidden) is unambiguous: before, the beam is a dark bar the width of the frame that a pilot at cruise cannot pick out of the starfield. It now carries a continuous emissive clearance stripe along the whole span, sixteen downward clearance chevrons, a `CLEARANCE BELOW` legend and nine pulsing red obstruction lamps — a lit line and a repeated shape, two channels, so the gate still reads with the colour taken out of it.

**Nothing in the range moved.** The header, both trusses and all four drones are frozen at their recorded positions by `tests/outbound_route_clearance_test.gd`, which fails if a later pass buys clearance by shifting them; every cue piece is presentation on the beam's own faces, adds no collider, and is checked to sit inside the beam's 8.5–9.5 m band so it cannot become drawn geometry standing in the lane it advertises. The suite also keeps the original defect reproducible: a Torrent on the old y = 8.0 aim must still be stopped by the gate. One defect in the cue itself was caught only by the render — a legend written 0.09 m "toward the viewer" on an axis that runs away from the station, so it was built 0.04 m inside the girder while every assertion passed — and there is now an assertion for that too.

**Still open on the first item:** packaged station-to-destination-to-station travel, human flight review, and broader save/network coverage. Race, patrol, Jovian delivery, Cinder platform supply, convoy escort, the derelict material scan, and the debris-beacon traversal now cross one GameFlow-owned generation fence into the existing atomic user-data file, recording a bounded aggregate and latest non-replayable return-incentive receipt while preserving unrelated namespaces (`tests/game_flow_reward_authority_test.gd`, 17 assertions). The Activity Board HUD shows that saved aggregate and latest receipt both immediately after completion and after a fresh startup; the physical Aft Operations console now mirrors the exact aggregate as `NO RETURNS FILED` or `N RETURNS FILED` before the player opens it. Both receive detached presentation data only and cannot grant rewards or infer currency/inventory (`tests/cinder_activity_integration_test.gd`, 39 assertions; `tests/activity_board_console_visual_test.gd`; `tests/cargo_activity_board_forward_render.gd`). This is a real packaged-data-capable completion reward, but deliberately not a currency wallet or proof of an economic payout. The Cinder cargo transfer is now a source-level production runtime loop and station defence remains a source-level production objective; neither replaces packaged-route or human evidence. The reusable foundations remain in `scripts/activities/`, `scripts/world/definitions/`, and the two Cinder Reach resources: `ActivityDirector` and `CheckpointRouteActivity` cover ordered beacon checkpoints, complete/fail/reset, and generation-safe stale-call rejection in `tests/activity_director_test.gd` (29 assertions), while `TimedCheckpointRace`, `CinderTimedRaceSession`, and `PatrolActivity` add timing/dwell and production composition without taking adjacent gameplay authority.

The previously orphaned eight-card Cinder activity directory is now reachable from that same player-facing Activity Board. At the shipyard it remains useful while the streamed cluster is correctly absent: race, patrol, extraction, scan, beacon, cargo, and convoy rows say `OUT OF RANGE // FLY TOWARD CINDER REACH TO LOAD` and disable lifecycle/persistence actions, while station defence remains live because its physical board is station-owned. Starting or resetting defence from the directory now delegates to that real board's on-foot `2.6 m` proximity and generation gates; a remote click changes no encounter state and gives explicit deck-board guidance, while an in-range click starts and confirmation-resets the physical encounter. Platform extraction now advances its real six-second timer only from the current production ship inside the authored `30 m` approach sphere: the flight HUD shows percentage and remaining hold time, leaving the sphere commits the existing interruption/reset state with zero retained progress, and completion writes the existing non-granting capacity receipt. A rejected store write remains visibly retryable from the same Start action without replaying the extraction timer or reward request. The scan's real Start action now begins a four-second ship hold at the authored derelict marker: leaving the `24 m` sphere pauses without losing progress, the flight HUD shows percentage/remaining time and return guidance, and completion either records the material-sample receipt or remains visibly retryable after a rejected store write. The debris-beacon Start action now drives the production ship through the four authored checkpoint spheres in strict order: the flight HUD names the next beacon and distance, skipping ahead cannot advance authority, and the terminal navigation-data receipt remains visibly retryable if its store write is rejected. The platform-supply Start action now opens the authored 120-second three-phase sortie for the exact Jovian occupying the production cargo berth. Caller physics automatically confirms the load only while docked, retains that ship's manifest across departure, accepts `clear_gate` only beyond the real assist-capture volume, and accepts `dock_platform` only when the same ship physically reoccupies the berth. Normal disembark authorizes the production Player against the current lease; walking to the existing terminal commits the real transfer receipt and shared fabrication-kit return record. Retained and flight HUDs show the current phase, deadline, and a color-independent Start-to-retry message if the reward store rejects without replaying inventory. Back/Escape and retained-tree focus return to the exact Activity Board route. The retained directory now also observes the coordinator's authoritative Cinder load, failure, and unload transitions: crossing the real `500 m` load radius enables the streamed cards immediately, and returning beyond the presentation-fade-gated `650 m` unload radius restores the honest disabled cards without requiring an activity event or page reopen. Focused coverage includes `tests/nearby_activity_game_flow_integration_test.gd` (34 assertions), `tests/nearby_activity_hud_integration_test.gd` (13 assertions), `tests/cinder_cargo_access_test.gd` (66 assertions), and `tests/cinder_cargo_urgency_retained_feedback_test.gd` (8 assertions); the parent board and unloaded directory were reviewed in real Forward+ at 1600×900. This improves discovery and access but does not close the packaged human route gate above.

The cargo-delivery prerequisite now also has a standalone typed foundation in `scripts/cargo/`: stable item definitions, bounded integer manifests bound to live entity/manifest generations, and atomic source-to-destination transfers with duplicate, stale, owner, quantity and capacity rejection. Detach/re-entry preserves one physical entity's manifest while retirement or deletion invalidates its handles. `CargoDeliveryContract` snapshots exact generation-bearing source/destination handles, item, quantity, ordered phases and a physics deadline; `CargoDeliveryActivity` completes only from the real authority's exact committed receipt, rejects replay/external consumption and signal re-entry, and requires an explicit generation reset after every terminal result (`tests/cargo_delivery_contract_test.gd`, 57 assertions). Production now exposes an existing-pause-menu Activity Board for race, patrol, and `Jovian Kit Delivery`; GameFlow binds the real Jovian and Jovian freight-berth nodes directly through one `CargoTransferAuthority`, advances a 180-second caller-physics deadline, records physical departure/return, and commits exactly two `fabrication_kits` only after the Jovian lands. The accepted receipt conserves stock **6 -> 4** on the ship and **0 -> 2** at the berth; reset, destruction, and expiry never refill it, and the terminal completion now records one separate non-replayable fabrication-kit return receipt (`tests/cargo_delivery_production_integration_test.gd`, 34 assertions). The streamed Cinder cluster now places the physical destination terminal and Jovian-compatible berth; its production `cinder_platform_supply_run` retains the exact source manifest while that Jovian leaves, advances the existing ordered phases from physical berth/gate facts, authorizes only the real disembarked Player/current lease, commits the existing terminal transfer, persists its terminal receipt, and shares the fabrication-kit reward counter without taking inventory or reward authority. Package, human, broader save/network, and complete return-route evidence remain open.

The Cinder side physical access module is now production-placed in the streamed cluster: a compatible Jovian `ShipBerth`, capture volume, collision-backed landing deck, three-step catwalk, exact live terminal handoff, and bidirectional production-Player route. Exact and off-centre public landing requests reach occupied/docked state through normal physics, and an occupied lease survives component detach/re-entry with stale attachment generations rejected. The focused production journey now also leaves the occupied lease, proves the still-inside-gate rejection, clears the authored capture volume, returns the same Jovian on a fresh lease, walks the production Player to/from the terminal without jumping, and fences transfer/reward replay (`tests/cinder_cargo_access_test.gd`, 65 assertions). This is source-level embodied route evidence, not a packaged or human-flown cargo-run claim.

The station-defence end of the sequence has the matching authority in `scripts/activities/`: bounded waves consume exact hostile identity+generation handles; caller physics delta advances delays/timeout; and protected-asset events remain detached generation-bearing data. `StationDefenseEncounterHost` composes the real `LiveCombatAuthority`, `CombatResolver`, `RangeOpponent`, and `LifecycleDamageableAdapter`, so resolver-terminal shots activate and complete waves without a parallel health/damage store. Production now places one physical Activity Board and one NEW/`modern_interpretation` encounter-content instance at the audited `(90, 0, -10)` anchor, coordinates the real player/fleet combat sources, protected-asset damage/failure/recovery, shared exactly-once reward handoff, reset, and terminal-history persistence. It adds no `GameFlow` phase and owns no duplicate combat/reward authority. Network, packaging, native and human play remain open, so the Phase 8 item stays unchecked.

The matching **production streaming path** now exists in `scripts/world/world_streaming_coordinator.gd`: registered `WorldLocationDefinition` scenes can be requested through an injectable asynchronous loader or an explicit `PackedScene` binding, with generation-stamped completion, deterministic coordinator-child placement at the definition's scene origin (separate from its navigation/activity anchor), lifecycle-safe unload/reload, failure recovery, and detach/re-entry identity held by `tests/world_streaming_coordinator_test.gd`. `CinderStreamingBootstrap` composes that coordinator with the explicit distance policy and checked Cinder resources: load at or inside 500 m, unload only beyond 650 m, one attempted transition per explicit update, and zero hidden process callbacks (`tests/cinder_streaming_bootstrap_test.gd`, 23 assertions). `Main` owns exactly one `CinderStreamingProductionBinding`, which samples the live piloted ship or Player once per physics tick and drives that explicit API. Station start and return retain zero Cinder instances; outbound commits one real `NearbySectorCluster`, whole-`Main` detach/re-entry keeps the same generation, and a later outbound trip creates exactly one new generation (`tests/cinder_streaming_production_journey_test.gd`). `ShipyardWorld.get_nearby_sector_cluster()` is consequently nullable and resolves only the coordinator-owned live instance. The streaming path still has no save/network, objective, reward, ship, berth, combat, or gameplay authority.

## Phase 9 — Release polish

### Design and implementation specification

- Treat release as a reproducible pipeline: clean source manifest → editor/import gate → complete isolated test matrix → graphical evidence/human review → release export → embedded-PCK inventory/metadata/signing inspection → packaged smoke → native hardware playtest → immutable checksums and release notes. A source test run never substitutes for package parity.
- Set measurable budgets on representative minimum/target Windows hardware: frame-time percentiles by graphics profile, CPU physics/script time, GPU time, memory/VRAM, draw calls/triangles/lights/particles, audio voices, package/startup time, network bandwidth where applicable, and long-session leak/orphan counts.
- Finish input/accessibility as systems, not labels: full keyboard/mouse and gamepad remapping, conflicts, deadzones/curves, hold/toggle choices, text/UI scaling, subtitles/captions, colour-safe cues, motion/camera comfort, ultrawide/safe areas, save/migration/reset, and controller-only completion of every required action.
- Harden packaging and recovery: signed executable/installer, versioned user-data schema, atomic settings/save writes, crash logging without secrets, safe fallback graphics/audio settings, missing/corrupt-data handling, reconnect/server-browser failure states, and uninstall/update behaviour.
- Release acceptance requires clean installs on supported desktop targets, first-run and upgrade tests, native-Windows uninterrupted solo and multiplayer sessions as applicable, representative performance, audible mix review, accessibility review, licence/permission clearance, signed artifacts, published checksums, and no open P0/P1 defects.

### Junior implementation playbook

1. Keep `RuntimeSettings` as validated settings state; add typed/versioned `input_binding_profile.gd`, `input_rebind_service.gd`, `user_data_store.gd`, and migration helpers. Use temp-write → flush/sync where supported → atomic replace; retain/recover the last valid document; reject unsupported newer schemas without overwriting them.
2. Implement remapping with action/device binding lists, conflict detection/resolution, deadzone/curve/hold-toggle data, defaults/reset, and UI focus. The controller help-overlay action now exists and a headless controller-only regression completes the solo loop, so remapping, conflict/reset UI, curves/hold-toggle execution and device glyphs have since landed; remaining work includes real-hardware focus and full required-route validation.
3. Add accessibility fields for subtitle/caption mode, text/UI scale, reticle/colour alternatives, camera shake, motion/flash reduction, and audio cue alternatives. Test default/round-trip/migration/reset and UI focus at 16:9, 16:10, 21:9, and 32:9 safe areas.
4. Add authored music/audio through checked-in assets, `ASSETS.md` provenance, fixed bus layout, and a `music_director.gd` that follows session/phase signals without owning gameplay. Verify packaged assets and perform real-device mix/audibility review.
5. Add `tools/release/` scripts for source manifest, editor/import, isolated matrix, graphical harness inventory, export, PE/PCK inventory, forbidden-path scan, smoke, hashes, and release notes. Each step writes a machine-readable result and fails closed; the orchestrator stops on the first invalid gate.
6. Inventory all current graphical harnesses and mark each `required`, `historical`, or `deprecated`; include player motion, combat visuals, Jovian berth, and Jovian freighter in addition to the currently documented runners. Required captures freeze source, validate image inventories, and receive original-resolution human review.
7. Add a benchmark runner with named scenarios and versioned budgets. Record hardware, OS/driver, resolution/profile, warm-up, p50/p95/p99/max frame time, CPU/GPU time, RAM/VRAM, draw/triangle/light/particle/voice counts, startup/package time, and network figures where applicable.
8. Give every artifact a unique semantic version plus build label and record source commit, matrix ID, Godot version, EXE/PCK size/hash/inventory, signing state, and smoke/native results. Never replace two different binaries under the same finalized/source-current label.
9. Keep signing/installer credentials outside repo/logs. Validate clean install, upgrade, rollback, corrupt-data recovery, crash-log redaction, uninstall, keyboard/mouse and controller-only play, audible mix, accessibility, performance, and multiplayer if shipped. Record remaining project/asset licensing and redistribution clearance before public distribution; a valid signature does not grant rights. The project owner has settled the original creator/rightsholder question (Phase 1, 2026-08-16); that decision remains in effect and is not reopened by this historical release checklist.

`MuddsShipyards-<7-character revision>.exe` displays that exact revision beside
the project version; editor runs say `SOURCE RUN`, and renamed or otherwise
unstamped packages say `UNSTAMPED BUILD` instead of inventing a source identity.
The footer is presentation-only and adds no controller focus stop. This closes
the in-game identification gap for future commit-named candidates, but it is not
a signature, immutable attestation, native-Windows run, or release-acceptance
claim (`tests/hud_panel_layout_test.gd`).

  A privacy-safe crash-diagnostic foundation now also exists in `scripts/diagnostics/`: `SessionDiagnosticRecord` retains a strict 64-event ring of fixed enum/primitive observations using caller-supplied session/physics timing, strips recognized secret fields, rejects paths/free text and malformed/nonfinite input, and produces deterministic detached JSON-safe snapshots. Optional restore/commit merges only `session_diagnostics` through an injected, already-loaded `UserDataStore`; it owns no clock, session/gameplay, settings/save, crash-recovery, filesystem-path, or commit-ID authority. `tests/session_diagnostic_record_test.gd` covers overflow, redaction, detach/re-entry and atomic-write failure. OS crash capture, production wiring, uploader/UI, stack traces, encryption, long-session tuning, package/native validation, and robust crash recovery remain open, so the Phase 9 item stays unchecked.

## Phase 10 — Final quality push and visitable planets

Complete these tracks in order. Do not hide a known stability or performance defect beneath additional world content.

### 1. Whole-game bug hunt and stabilization

The first focused audit wave has already closed several concrete production defects without treating that as an end-to-end playthrough: cargo source/destination reattachment is now one atomic, generation-safe transaction under synchronous removal and signal re-entry; orderly HUD/window exit enters the existing safe-start clean-shutdown seam before quitting; settings profiles reach all nine retained ship input banks atomically, including the three deferred expansion craft; and whole-`Main` re-entry restores the exact retained pause/settings/activity focus target instead of leaving controller navigation unfocused or jumping Activity Back to Timed Race. Active activities now terminalize on pilot unseating and active-hull replacement even when Cinder is already fading or Main has detached/re-entered, rather than leaking non-convoy cargo/activity generations. ### 2. Measured performance improvement

The current merged trim pass now changes production cost rather than extending
evidence families. Repeated inert visuals share immutable resources across the
Arrow, Jovian, Bulwark, Cinder, opponent, station-service and planetary
presentation families; bounded `MultiMesh` batches retain authored copies while
reducing submissions throughout Fleet Dock, Habitat, Aft, Fabrication, VIP,

Ember surface presentation. Five berth-feedback displays replace thirty
duplicate box meshes with five shared unit-box resources, and five station doors
replace twenty presentation meshes with four immutable recipes. Disabled station
machinery ambience avoids twelve idle synthesized streams / 335,360 PCM bytes
across four zones, while final-approach audio uses one retained semantic voice
instead of two. Focused feature tests preserve collision, interaction, lifecycle
and gameplay authority; these source-side deltas do **not** claim native draw
calls, GPU/VRAM/frame time, audibility or human visual-review completion.

Observation and Salvage now remove `60 m²` each of redundant outer walkable strips while
preserving their route seams, ramps, collision-backed pads, markers, rails and traversal.
Their walkable footprints change from `426 -> 366 m²` and `456 -> 396 m²`, a combined
`120 m²` reduction. Native-Windows frame, GPU and VRAM measurement remains `NOT_RUN`.

### 4. Visitable planets with complete atmosphere-to-surface loops

The first contract layer has landed without claiming a visitable planet. `PlanetaryWorldDefinition` freezes destination identity, scene/navigation/orbital/surface frames, atmosphere/terrain/landing references and evidence status; `PlanetaryAtmosphereProfile` freezes explicit metre/SI density, optical, fog, cloud, weather, entry-effect and audio-hint fields; and `PlanetaryTerrainProfile` freezes elevation, clipmap/collision LOD, tile ceilings, biome ordering, landing tolerances and floating-origin thresholds. `PlanetaryWorldCompositionValidator` joins those three around one exact **120,000 m centre-to-sea-level datum**, rejects mismatched IDs/radii, terrain above the atmosphere shell and invalid scene/surface/orbital/navigation radii, and treats its documented endpoints inclusively. `PlanetaryCoordinateFrame` represents absolute orbital positions as safe integer cells plus canonical metre offsets, subtracts cells before float composition, and exposes generation-stamped caller-owned rebase translations without moving a node itself. `PlanetaryLandingRegionDefinition` adds bounded body-local approach boxes, touchdown pads, compatibility tags, on-foot egress, surface-route anchors, slope/roughness and clearance data; its +Y basis must point along the outward radial while retaining arbitrary tangent yaw. `PlanetaryLandingCompositionValidator` binds that region to the world's landing roster, terrain profile, configured body frame, exact radius/elevation datum and canonical absolute-orbital representation, and freezes a rebase witness in which absolute position remains stable while world-local position changes by the committed translation.

`PlanetaryAtmosphereSampler` derives bounded density, transmittance,
visibility/fog, cloud, wind and entry-effect samples from a copied validated
profile. Three passive renderer adapters consume only caller-owned targets:
`PlanetaryAtmospherePresentation` transactionally owns four supplied
`Environment` fog properties; `PlanetarySkyPresentation` owns only top and two
horizon colours on an existing `ProceduralSkyMaterial`; and
`PlanetaryCloudPresentation` owns six reflected uniforms on an existing
compatible `ShaderMaterial`. The cloud adapter does **not** create cloud
geometry, shader code, noise, shadows or a visible production layer.
`PlanetarySunLightingPolicy` evaluates a spherical elevated horizon,
airless/vacuum terminator and bounded atmospheric twilight into normalized
unitless hints only—no lux, star spectrum, ephemeris, terrain/cloud shadow or
renderer mutation. `PlanetarySunPresentation` may transactionally multiply an
existing caller-authored `DirectionalLight3D` baseline colour and energy by
those hints, with exact rollback/detach restoration; it never orients the light
or claims clock, ephemeris, shadow, occlusion, calibrated colour or lux.
`PlanetarySurfaceAudioPolicy` similarly returns opaque
exterior/interior route IDs, endpoint mix, base/attenuation values and a
density/airflow intensity hint; it resolves no asset and owns no playback,
mixer, clock or audio authority. The passive entry-heat foundation owns one
normalized uniform on an exclusive collision-free overlay target; Arrow now
hosts exactly one such target beneath its final visual root, but the target
remains unconfigured at exact zero because no production atmospheric profile
or observation caller exists. A separate Ember airless-sun rig/binding
foundation composes the normalized sun policy and two-property light adapter
against exact streamed Ember identities, but it is also standalone and has no
Main/GameFlow caller. These are coherent foundations, not a complete
atmosphere, and no authored atmospheric production world consumes them yet.

**Superseded description — `aurora_temperate_world` is a visitable production world; the paragraph below describes the state when it was written and misled a later reading into thinking it was still only a witness.** It was a separate, explicitly non-production
atmospheric witness: matching 120 km world/terrain/atmosphere/landing resources
join through both composition validators, and its standalone composition is the
sole `WorldEnvironment` owner. Its body-centred scene now owns the first bounded
runtime terrain generator rather than only a flat proxy: five caller-built
65 × 65 spherical clipmap rings produce **21,125 vertices / 40,096 visible
triangles**, one shared biome-band material and one **32,768-triangle**
relief-matched collision shape reaching the profile's 1.5 km physical boundary.
The complete authored approach corridor stays inside a 750 m
flat envelope, the 94 m centre opening exposes the existing landing-floor disc,
and the 48 m collision opening hands support to the existing 96 m walkable patch
without coplanar fighting. Generation, rebuild and retirement are fenced;
detach retains the committed terrain, a different radial focus rebuilds the
same bounded roster, and no camera or automatic cadence was added. The live
Shipyard backdrop's former plain green sphere now also uses one authored Aurora
ocean/land/cloud/atmospheric-limb shader while retaining the same single draw
submission and zero gameplay authority. Aurora still has no streaming, Player,
production focus caller, navigation, gameplay or Main/GameFlow route, and its
detached pad-to-staging audit remains non-traversable, so neither presentation
slice makes it visitable.

`PlanetaryTerrainLodPolicy` selects inclusive near-to-far render/collision
rings and exposes only bounded tile-ceiling hints. `PlanetarySurfaceGravityPolicy`
supplies pure body-local radial up, inward inverse-square gravity and tangent

world-space vector to `HeroShip`; the ship consumes it once inside its existing
flight integration, keeps sole velocity/`move_and_slide()` authority, and uses

world and landing reports into a caller-physics
orbit/entry/descent/surface/landing/on-foot/take-off/ascent/return state
machine. `PlanetaryCruisePolicy` now publishes a strict 20,000 m/s recommendation
with current-generation full-hull swept-corridor proof, exact acceleration and
braking envelopes, and no movement authority. The standalone
`PlanetaryCruisePhysicalController` plus `HeroShip` integration turns one fresh
proof into real acceleration, overspeed braking and collision-safe movement;
the ship remains the sole velocity and `move_and_slide()` owner, stale/forged
proofs fail closed, and the bounded sweep horizon is 750 km. Main now owns one
production binding and one stable controller; GameFlow queues at most one
envelope after the common-origin transaction from the same adjusted actor
sample, and Hero consumes it on the next physics tick. The pause menu exposes
both the controller-reachable fixed `EMBER CRUISE` engage/disengage row and a
retained Destination Board backed by a two-world catalog. Ember is the sole
routed/actionable entry and reports its exact 8,000 km distance, itinerary and

its action disabled. The previously decorative Aft Operations Console Bay 01
is now a readable physical Destination Board terminal: it mirrors the retained
two-world/one-route count plus Ember's public status and opens that exact HUD
page through ordinary on-foot interaction. It survives Main detach/re-entry
with one signal binding and cannot select or launch a route
(`tests/planetary_destination_console_production_test.gd`, 9 assertions). A

existing generation-fenced expedition toggle instead of creating another
travel path. The retained Ember journey owns one surface handoff and fixed
Mudds Shipyards return target; the existing cruise, manual-landing and berth
authorities own arrival rather than a parallel mover. No new raw-input,
ship-command, movement, streaming, origin, landing, activity, reward, save or

- [ ] Turn the nearby coloured bodies into authored, visitable destinations rather than decorative spheres. Begin with one vertical slice planet or moon and complete it before multiplying worlds: orbital approach, atmospheric entry where applicable, descent, surface flight, landing, on-foot traversal, activities, take-off, ascent, orbit, and return to Mudds Shipyards without a loading/lifecycle dead end.
- [ ] Build a reusable planetary-world contract covering scale and coordinate frames, streaming/origin management, terrain LOD and collision, biome/material layers, atmosphere and sky scattering, clouds, weather, wind, fog, day/night and sun/moon lighting, water where appropriate, surface audio, navigation, landing sites, settlements/structures, hazards, wildlife only if deliberately authored, and save/session persistence.
- [ ] Make atmosphere physically and visually coherent for the chosen game scale: space-to-sky transition, horizon and aerial perspective, density/visibility change with altitude, cloud layers and shadows, entry heat/compression effects, wind/weather response, and distinct interior/exterior audio. Approximation is expected, but the model, units, transitions, and performance trade-offs must be documented and stable. **Aurora altitude slice, 2026-09-23 (`c1ab8bcd1`):** above the 20 km atmosphere top the orbital sky is dark, fog is absent and ambient fill is reduced; descent smoothly restores coastal sky, ambient light and fog. Solar/weather recipe updates and scene re-entry preserve altitude attenuation. The production-scene high/mid/surface state test and existing atmosphere, Aurora and Ember checks passed headlessly. Rendered human judgement, native GPU cost, entry heat, weather wind response and interior/exterior sound transitions remain open.
- [ ] Give each visitable world meaningful authored content: recognisable orbital silhouette, at least one substantial landing region, multiple navigable landmarks, surface routes, activities/rewards tied to existing authority systems, recoverable failure states, and a reason to return. Do not expand into procedural emptiness or duplicate the station's role. **Ember caldera became a place, 2026-09-20 (bbf8c8f5e, and offered in game by 129df9542 → dfe547e7a):** the caldera had one errand and one walk; it now has three landmarks a player can see from the pad and walk to on marked chevron routes — a low lava-tube arch 88 m west, a 19.5 m survey mast 93 m north and a tipped lander wreck 82 m south-east, each a real solid on terrain collision with its own approach marker — and two more bounded errands beside the relay survey, a lava-tube sounding and a lander-wreck survey, whose checkpoints sit out on those routes so neither can be satisfied from the pad. Each pays once through the existing reward authority, survives a mid-visit save and a re-entry, and abandons without touching the craft, the berth lease or the way home. Both are offered in game from authored trailheads: an `ERRAND AVAILABLE` billboard and the ordinary on-foot interact prompt, which substitutes the live glyph so it reads the pad button on a controller; taking one turns that point into the abandon and removes the other from the interaction layer so it can never steal the press the pilot needs to get back aboard, and the standing surface card carries the logged count and the live distance to the next checkpoint. Nothing appears aboard a craft or off Ember, and the trailheads anchor to the live authored region so a world-origin rebase carries them with it. Cost: 636 triangles and 23 nodes on the streamed Ember generation, no lights; the six-cycle soak stayed flat on every counter. Routes were verified empirically — terrain is continuous and level to within 4 cm from the patch edge outward, and the furthest point is inside the recentre distance, so walking the region never triggers a terrain rebuild. **Two unreachable interactions fixed 2026-09-20 (9360b83b4, d2447d706), found by building the trailheads:** the authored sample rack and survey bunker presses set their position from a body-local value while parented under a plain composition node that is not in the body frame, so both stood 120,012 m above the caldera floor — measured in the production Main-composed path on both visits, not inferred. In a packaged build `ANALYSE SAMPLE RACK` and `LOG BUNKER / GANTRY SURVEY` could never be reached, and the bunker published that same position as its service terminal, so the terminal repair could only ever answer out-of-range. Both now anchor to the live authored region and re-anchor on re-entry, landing within a metre of the authored spot, with the check that would have caught it added to two suites. Separately the relay survey's landing-pad guides had never bound at all: the binding read the loaded scene id at the top level of the Host snapshot while the Host publishes it under `identities`, so it silently resolved nothing; the guides now cant, restore and lower with survey state as their own readability suite always specified. Their collision boxes stay upright by design, documented rather than given collision authority to a presentation node. The fixture that hid this published the id in both places, unlike the real Host, and now publishes it only where the Host does. **The whole class swept 2026-09-20 (96678d257, c0431d029):** the composition is a plain `Node`, so a child's position is in neither authored frame — thirteen further placements were measured wrong in the production Main path and fixed, the relay and return survey markers and the reward seal at 120,021 to 120,042 m, four settlement practicals, two landing approaches, the relay-arc hazard zone with its perimeter and beacon, and the water surface, all now standing within a metre of their authored heights. Eight landmark beacons and the surface route trail showed the subtler half of the same bug: their authored values carry no body radius, so they were region-local readings floating in the composition frame, measured 12.445 m up on that descent and arbitrarily far off mid-flight. One mechanism now anchors every cue through the frame its authored value actually means, body-centred or region-relative, re-anchored on re-entry; the orbital approach ring deliberately stays body-framed because its anchor means an altitude above the moon's centre, and it now measures exactly its authored 20 km instead of 120 km past it. A single family sweep in both live-caldera suites requires every visible or collidable node the composition places to stand near the floor and to be anchored to an authored frame at all, and it names all thirteen if the fix is reverted. **A save-corruption bug fell out of it:** the whole-Main teardown save asked detached actors for their world transforms, which answer identity out of tree, so it wrote a checkpoint with the pilot, the craft and the berth at the world origin and, in the soak's own save leg, overwrote the correct save committed a line earlier. Nothing asserted the teardown save, and every suite exercising it called it in tree. The collector now refuses while the host, player or berth have left the tree, which also removes all 63 engine errors the soak had been printing per run.
- [ ] Prove the full loop with production Player and ships on minimum and target profiles: no precision jitter, terrain tunnelling, floating-origin discontinuity, atmosphere pop, stranded player/ship, broken moving-interior state, invalid landing support, unbounded streaming growth, or save/re-entry divergence. Include controller-only navigation, packaged native-Windows review, and long-session orbit↔surface repetition. **Partially closed 2026-09-15:** `tests/ember_loop_soak_evidence.gd` drives production Main through the real Ember expedition — board, launch, `begin_ember_surface_journey`, streamed moon load, common-world rebase, cruise approach, caldera landing through the real berth lease, disembark, authored egress route on live terrain, re-board attempt — with per-tick discontinuity, altitude, support, presentation and streaming counters. It found and fixed four production defects: a committed origin rebase aborted the landing it was in the middle of (`berth_changed` on every descent, since the caldera drop is exactly the 10 km rebase threshold), the cruise binding discarded the approach on the tick the craft arrived, an admitted expedition never re-armed its approach (stranded in orbit), and the caldera berth stayed configured for the first craft that ever landed. Measured on the loop that now completes: 1 rebase of 10,000.063 m with a 12.5 m largest single-tick step against a 334 m bound, 922 on-foot ticks with 0 unsupported and a +0.001 m minimum tangent altitude, 0 presentation deltas, streamed nodes 83 → 0 after departure, save/re-entry drift 0.000 m, flat counters over 18 cycles. **Recorded boundaries, not closed:** re-boarding is gated by the ~570 m relay survey (so take-off, ascent, orbital return and the yard landing are not exercised), no production caller starts the expedition (the pause nav toggle only engages cruise), an expedition cannot be abandoned, a whole-Main re-entry on the surface terminalises the host, and a repeat visit is never re-admitted (`docs/EMBER_LOOP_SOAK.md`). **Closed 2026-09-15 (595d9f93a, 04b109a60, 80731decd):** the pause `EMBER CRUISE` row and the Destination Board had in fact started the real expedition since 87400dc49; they now also publish the standing `EMBER EXPEDITION` HUD objective and the activity briefing channel. A live expedition can be abandoned from the same row, on craft loss, or by a terminal Host: the survey generation ends with no reward, the caldera lease and command return to their owners, the retained Host resets in place, and the craft flies home on the same Mudds return approach the completed loop uses; an abandon asked while the craft is on or committed to the pad is *pending* — the outbound route and re-board gate lift, the pilot walks back, boards, and the Host's own takeoff commits it — so no pilot is ever separated from their craft. Repeat visits are re-admitted by the same retained `Main` with the same Host/binding identities (three production defects fixed: the Host and travel session now reset in place, a Host left on a streamed-out world is rebound never under a live expedition, and the coordinator adopts the binding's visit-scoped caller-serial fence, which was silently refusing every cadence tick of visit two). A whole-Main save/re-entry on the surface now suspends the visit intact instead of terminalising it (the loss-vs-re-entry decision is taken one deferred step later, from the composition root's tree membership) and resuming re-asserts the planetary gravity binding and seat claim. `EmberMoonStreamingBootstrap` implements the common-world translation seam, curing the sub-millimetre `bootstrap_alignment_invalid` that starved the surface cadence after an 8,000 km rebase. Six-cycle soak: 122 assertions, cycles 2/4/6 are genuine second/third/fourth expeditions, counters identical across all six cycles, 3 re-entries with 0 terminal Hosts, 0 reward receipts. **Landing closed 2026-09-15 (731cbda6f):** it was never a repeat-visit defect — cycles 2/4/6 shared the Torrent. Defect 1's fix re-expressed the frozen dock snapshot by adding the rebase delta while the live berth re-derives its dock through its parent chain, and at 10 km float32 rounds the two apart by 0.078 mm for the Arrow but 0.391 mm for the Torrent (0.775 m dock height) against the absolute 0.1 mm landing epsilon, so every Torrent descent aborted `berth_changed` inside its own rebase. `HeroShip.notify_common_world_translation()` now re-expresses the dock and staging targets from the live berth wherever it agrees with the translated snapshot within a relative rounding budget (2^-20 of the largest magnitude, floored at the epsilon); the exact guard stays exact afterwards and a 1 cm unannounced berth move still aborts. Proven with exact production geometry for both craft in `landing_clearance_test`, a new retained-Main Arrow-then-Torrent `ember_repeat_visit_landing_test` (31 assertions, one owner rebase per descent, dock snapshot exact on the live berth), and the six-cycle soak: all six cycles now land, disembark, walk the route, reach the survey gate and abandon (167 assertions, counters identical every cycle, 3 re-entries, 0 terminal Hosts). **Physical travel subsequently landed:** commits `719d28abf` and `8a5cb9e69` carry fresh Ember outbound and homeward return through the shared physical cruise path, committed origin rebases, actual caldera touchdown and ordinary home berth approach. Keep Mudds Shipyards the social and logistical heart of the game. **First extraction landed 2026-09-20 (b618f12b2, 00f15f690):** an attempt to make Aurora visitable found it already was — it registers on the Destination Board, flies the player out, lands through a real berth lease, disembarks onto its own terrain and returns, proven end to end by a 42-assertion suite, while the roadmap prose above and its own doc still called it a non-production witness. What was genuinely missing is now closed: an Aurora visit interrupted by a whole-Main re-entry used to end silently, putting the pilot back at Mudds with no record they had gone, and now returns them standing on Aurora beside the same craft on the same pad with a real lease. `PlanetaryStreamingBootstrap` is the first real extraction — datum lookup, frame configuration, location registration, absolute-focus evaluation with its hysteresis, travel encoding, committed-rebase re-expression and the snapshot scaffolding — with a subclass supplying one profile; Ember's airless sun rig, environment presentation and scene identity stay Ember's, and all 58 Ember suites passed on the extraction commit alone. Aurora reads differently on arrival because it composes its own atmosphere: fog, an atmospheric horizon and a cloud deck over a coast with a gravel trail, a signed lookout deck, standing stones, groves and a live waterline, at 207 nodes and 78,374 triangles against Ember's 106 and 40,420. **Still open and deliberately not attempted:** Aurora does not use the cruise binding, journey coordinator, world-streaming coordinator or origin-rebase owner — its outbound leg is still an explicit jump — because the rebase owner binds exactly one bootstrap pair at ready and is statically typed to Ember's classes, as is the cruise binding's final-approach request. **Done 2026-09-21 (1fa0e88ef, 37d77c65c, eada5fd40).** The rebase owner no longer names Ember: it scans its host for every planetary production binding, pairs each with the bootstrap that binding resolved and that bootstrap's own coordinate frame, keys the roster by world id, routes each transaction by the world the preview names and refuses an unknown one, and offers fenced bind, unbind and rebind. The `EmberSurfaceLoopHost` special case became a capability a node declares rather than a class the owner knows. The cruise binding resolves its bootstrap by the shared base type and takes its destination and canonical coordinate from that bootstrap's own registered location, and its final-approach request accepts anything publishing a readiness snapshot, so Ember's phase enum no longer appears in it. The shared production binding was extracted too, leaving each world's binding about thirty lines naming itself. **Composing a second world immediately exposed a latent defect:** a transaction advanced only the requesting world's frame, translating the other world's root out from under a frame still describing the old origin, so Aurora would have broken the instant an Ember expedition launched. A transaction now opens a pending rebase on every bound frame, all or none, commits the requesting world first while everything is still reversible, and fails closed if any other refuses. Aurora now flies the real lane: coordinator admission, its own streaming observation, committed origin rebases (unavoidable at 12,000 km against a 10 km threshold), an armed authored approach corridor, a real berth lease on the streamed scene, and a rebase home that streams the world out behind the craft. **Subsequent physical-travel work, 2026-09-22 (`bc38358ef`):** fresh Aurora outbound and RETURN now fly through the shared cruise and approach controllers without those staging placements; interrupted-visit restoration and explicit surface rescue retain recovery placement. The same Halyard completed 12,011.876 km outbound with 1,163 origin shifts, then 12,113.017 km home with 1,174 further shifts, full hull, continuous pilot ownership, a real home berth lease and docking. The first full run failed its final on-foot support assertion because the test walked backward from the port exit into the authored apron gap. The corrected along-apron run reached the same home berth, docked, and walked 1.548 m with floor support: its log ended with 14 passing assertions after 24,124.893 km and 2,337 origin shifts. The original failed report remains retained; the corrected process exit code was unavailable after session interruption. The landing controller also now preserves parent/local composition order across rebases, fixing the measured 8.8 mm disagreement that retired an earlier final approach. These results do not close native performance, controller-only, human-review or repeated whole-game endurance gates.
